findings.title: Checkpoint/rollback silently destroys untracked files (git clean -fd on state never captured)
findings.description: git:createCheckpoint (main.ts:432-449) uses `git stash create`, which captures ONLY tracked modifications — untracked files are not in the stash object. git:rollback (main.ts:452-467) then runs `git checkout .` + `git clean -fd` + `git stash apply`. `git clean -fd` permanently deletes every untracked file — including files that existed (untracked) at checkpoint time and were never captured. For an app whose whole pitch is letting AI agents write files (which are usually untracked until committed), 'rollback' is a data shredder. There is no confirmation, no dry-run, no backup, and if `stash apply` fails the tree has already been wiped by the two preceding commands.
findings.recommendation: Capture untracked state at checkpoint time (e.g. build a temporary index with GIT_INDEX_FILE + `git add -A` + `git write-tree`/`git commit-tree` onto a hidden ref, WezTerm/jj-style snapshotting), and on rollback restore from that tree instead of running `git clean -fd`. At minimum: never run `clean -fd` unless the checkpoint provably contains the untracked set, and move deleted files to a trash dir first.

findings.title: Zero PTY output flow control or coalescing — one webContents.send per node-pty chunk
findings.description: pty.onData fires mainWindow?.webContents.send(`pty:data:${id}`, data) for every raw chunk with no batching, no pause/resume, and no acknowledgement. A command that spews MBs (a build log, `type bigfile`, an agent dumping a diff) generates tens of thousands of IPC messages; each one triggers the renderer's extremely heavy per-chunk handler (src/hooks/usePty.ts:759-830: regex masking, ANSI stripping, provider detection, a Zustand store append, and a `window[bufferKey]` write per chunk) plus an unbounded xterm.js write queue. node-pty exposes IPty.pause()/resume() and xterm's write() callback exists exactly for this handshake — none of it is used. Result: renderer event-loop flooding, GC churn, seconds-long UI freezes, and unbounded memory growth under load. main.ts:41-44's 'crisp WebGL rendering' switches cannot compensate for a firehose with no valve.
findings.recommendation: Coalesce PTY output in main on an ~8-16 ms flush timer (concat chunks, single send), and implement the standard xterm flow-control pattern: count unacknowledged bytes, pty.pause() past a high-water mark, resume() when the renderer acks via xterm write callbacks. Route all sessions over one multiplexed 'pty:data' channel with {id, data} instead of per-session dynamic channels.

findings.title: sandbox:false + unrestricted filesystem/exec IPC surface with zero sender validation
findings.description: webPreferences sets sandbox:false (main.ts:185) even though nothing in preload.ts requires it (contextBridge and webUtils both work sandboxed). Meanwhile the IPC surface hands the renderer: read/write/delete/rename of ANY path on disk (fs:createFile 470, fs:delete 525, fs:readFile 548 — no scoping to a workspace root), arbitrary shell spawn via pty:create with a caller-supplied `shell` string (256-293), arbitrary executable execution via cli:getVersion/cli:discoverModels (710-731), and destructive git operations. Not a single handler checks event.senderFrame or event.sender — any code that gains renderer execution (one XSS in the terminal UI, a malicious ANSI/OSC payload rendered into a React component, a compromised dependency) instantly owns the user's account. Defense-in-depth here is zero: the contextIsolation baseline is right but everything behind the bridge is a skeleton key.
findings.recommendation: Enable sandbox:true, validate event.senderFrame.url === main window URL in every ipcMain handler (a small wrapper/router), and scope all fs:* handlers to registered workspace roots (resolve + prefix-check against allowed dirs). Treat pty:create's shell as an enum of validated shells plus explicit user-configured paths, not a free-form string.

findings.title: force-device-scale-factor=1 breaks every high-DPI Windows machine
findings.description: app.commandLine.appendSwitch('force-device-scale-factor', '1') forces Chromium to treat every display as 96 DPI. On the typical 125-150 % scaled Windows laptop (i.e., most of them), the entire app renders tiny — text, hit targets, terminal cells — and per-monitor DPI switching is dead. The adjacent 'high-dpi-support' switch (line 43) has been obsolete/removed from Chromium for years and does nothing. The comment claims this is for 'crisp WebGL terminal rendering'; WezTerm handles DPI properly per-monitor and stays crisp. This is a self-inflicted, app-wide visual bug on the app's primary platform.
findings.recommendation: Delete both switches (lines 43-44). If WebGL glyph blurriness at fractional scales was the original motivation, fix it in the renderer by sizing the canvas with devicePixelRatio (xterm's WebGL addon already does) rather than lying to the compositor about the display.

findings.title: Recreating a session with the same id can deliver the OLD process's exit event to the NEW session
findings.description: PtyManager.create() kills any existing process with the same id (pty-manager.ts:153-156). The manager guards its map against stale exits (pty-manager.ts:212-216), but main.ts's per-create closures do not: the old process's onExit handler (main.ts:284-286) still fires — asynchronously on Windows/ConPTY — and sends on the SAME channel `pty:exit:${id}` that the new session's renderer listener has by then subscribed to (registration happens after the awaited pty:create resolves, usePty.ts:1462). The renderer then prints '[Process exited]', finalizes the active block, and marks the agent offline while the new PTY is alive and well. Same hazard exists for late `pty:data:${id}` chunks from the dying old process bleeding into the new terminal.
findings.recommendation: Attach a generation counter (or the pid) to each create; include it in every pty:data/pty:exit payload and have the renderer discard mismatches — or store the IDisposables returned by onData/onExit in PtyManager and dispose the old process's handlers before killing it.

findings.title: Everything spawns through cmd.exe with hand-rolled quoting — %VAR% expansion and .cmd-shim re-parsing survive it
findings.description: getSpawnSpec (runtime-utils.ts:25-35) routes ALL runCommand calls on Windows — including plain `git` — through `cmd.exe /d /s /c` with a homemade quoteWindowsArgument (19-23) that doubles quotes and wraps on metacharacters. This is fragile three ways: (1) cmd expands %VAR% and delayed-expansion !var! even inside double quotes, so argument content can smuggle environment expansion; (2) `""` escaping is interpreted differently by cmd vs CommandLineToArgvW vs the batch re-parse that npm's claude.cmd/gemini.cmd shims perform, and cli:getVersion/cli:discoverModels feed renderer-controlled command strings straight into this path (main.ts:710-731, gated only by normalizeCommandInput stripping wrapping quotes); (3) on timeout, child.kill() (runtime-utils.ts:106-113) terminates cmd.exe but NOT its grandchildren on Windows — a hung `git fetch` or CLI keeps running orphaned.
findings.recommendation: Spawn real executables directly with shell:false: resolve npm .cmd shims once via `where`/reading the shim to the underlying node script, call git.exe directly. For timeout kill, use taskkill /PID <pid> /T /F or assign children to a Job Object so the whole tree dies.

findings.title: Swarm lock 'atomicity' is fake — read-modify-write TOCTOU across await points, comment claims otherwise
findings.description: The doc comment (line 81) says 'Uses atomic write (tmp + rename) to prevent TOCTOU race conditions', but tmp+rename only makes the final WRITE atomic. acquireLocks (83-116) does readLockFile → conflict check → mutate → write with awaits between each step; two concurrent swarm:acquireLocks IPC invocations (which interleave freely in the main process) can both read the same registry, both pass the conflict check for the same file, and the second write silently clobbers the first agent's locks — the exact race the feature exists to prevent. Bonus: releaseLocks (122-159) and forceReleaseLocks (184-223) are near-identical duplicated logic, and forceReleaseLocks' comment ('Unlike releaseLocks, this does not require the caller to be the lock owner') describes a difference that doesn't exist — neither checks ownership. forceReleaseLocks and getStaleLocks are exported and never called by anything.
findings.recommendation: Serialize all lock operations per swarmRoot through an in-process promise queue (mutex) in the main process; if out-of-process agents also touch file-locks.json, use an O_EXCL sentinel lockfile around the read-modify-write. Merge release/forceRelease into one function and delete the dead exports.

findings.title: No Windows process-tree cleanup — killed PTYs can leave zombie children, and nothing kills PTYs on quit paths other than window-all-closed
findings.description: kill() calls proc.kill() which closes the ConPTY; console-attached processes usually die, but background/detached children spawned by the shell or by agent CLIs (node servers, watchers the agent launched) survive as orphans. WezTerm-class terminals put the child in a Job Object precisely for this. Additionally, ptyManager.killAll() runs only in 'window-all-closed' (main.ts:825-830); a crash of the main process, or quit flows that bypass that event, leave whole shell trees running. isAlive() (pty-manager.ts:266-279) also uses process.kill(pid, 0), which on Windows can false-positive after PID reuse.
findings.recommendation: Create a Job Object per PTY (JOB_OBJECT_LIMIT_KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE) via a small native helper or use taskkill /PID /T /F in kill(); also call killAll() from app 'before-quit' and 'will-quit' so every exit path reaps children.

findings.title: PowerShell silently forced to -NoProfile and -ExecutionPolicy Bypass
findings.description: withShellStartupArgs (46-65) injects -NoLogo, -NoProfile, and -ExecutionPolicy Bypass into every PowerShell/pwsh session unless the user happened to pass those flags themselves. In an interactive terminal this means the user's $PROFILE (aliases, prompt, PSReadLine config, conda/nvm init) silently never loads — a class of 'why does my shell behave differently in this app' bugs — and execution policy is bypassed without consent, weakening a machine-level security setting as a hidden side effect. parseShell's regex tokenizer (29-39) is also fragile: an unquoted 'C:\Program Files\PowerShell\7\pwsh.exe' splits into two tokens and spawns the wrong file.
findings.recommendation: Load profiles by default like every real terminal; make -NoProfile and execution-policy overrides explicit opt-in settings. Replace the regex tokenizer with a real path check (statSync the full string first, then fall back to tokenizing).

findings.title: ConPTY→winpty fallback only catches synchronous spawn errors; stale comment contradicts the actual strategy
findings.description: The spawn-plan loop (198-205) falls back (ConPTY → winpty → default shell) only when pty.spawn THROWS synchronously. In practice ConPTY failures (AttachConsole errors, agent startup crashes) frequently surface asynchronously — the spawn returns an IPty that immediately exits or emits on the exit event — so the fallback chain almost never actually engages for the failure mode it was built for; the user just gets a dead terminal. Meanwhile the comment at line 161 still says 'Use winpty on Windows to avoid conpty AttachConsole errors in Electron' while the code at 136-146 deliberately prefers ConPTY — a stale contradiction left from an earlier iteration.
findings.recommendation: Detect early-death (exit within ~500 ms with nonzero code or zero output) and respawn with the next plan; surface which backend won to the renderer for diagnostics. Delete the stale comment.

findings.title: Dead code across all three layers: workspace IPC + WorkspaceManager, pty:getCwd, unused lock exports
findings.description: WorkspaceManager (workspace-manager.ts:6-52), its three IPC handlers (main.ts:351-361), and the preload wrappers (preload.ts:53-55) are referenced only by the type declaration in src/lib/types.ts — no renderer code ever calls workspaceSave/Load/List. pty:getCwd is triple-plumbed (pty-manager.ts:238-263, main.ts:311-313, preload.ts:18) yet never invoked, and on Windows — the app's only shipped target per electron-builder.yml — it unconditionally returns null anyway. swarm-file-lock-manager's forceReleaseLocks/getStaleLocks (184-244) have zero callers. Every dead IPC channel is free attack surface plus maintenance noise.
findings.recommendation: Delete WorkspaceManager, the workspace:* and pty:getCwd channels, and the unused lock exports; or wire them up if session-restore was supposed to use them. Keep the IPC surface exactly as large as the feature set.

findings.title: Non-atomic writes for storage:set and workspace save — the atomic util exists in-repo but isn't reused
findings.description: storage:set (main.ts:606-618) and WorkspaceManager.save (workspace-manager.ts:24) write JSON with a direct fs.writeFile. A crash, power loss, or the 3-second force-destroy during the close handshake landing mid-write leaves a truncated file; storage:get (599-603) then swallows the JSON.parse error and returns null, silently wiping the user's persisted tabs/settings. Ironically swarm-file-lock-manager.ts:53-74 already implements exactly the right tmp+rename-with-EPERM-retry pattern — it just isn't shared, so the codebase has one correct and two incorrect persistence paths (duplicated logic, inconsistently applied).
findings.recommendation: Extract writeLockFileAtomic into a shared atomicWriteJson(path, data) util and use it for storage:set and workspace saves; optionally keep a .bak of the last good file and fall back to it on parse failure.

findings.title: Windows env merge is case-sensitive — duplicate PATH/Path keys with undefined precedence
findings.description: create() spreads process.env then overlays options.env with plain object assignment (164-183). Windows env names are case-insensitive, but JS objects aren't: if the renderer sends env.PATH while process.env holds 'Path', the child's environment block gets BOTH entries and which one the OS honors is undefined — classic 'my CLI can't be found only inside GhostShell' bug. The dangerous-key blocklist (line 177) is a good instinct but blocklists always trail reality (e.g. ComSpec, PSModulePath, PATHEXT manipulation all pass through).
findings.recommendation: On win32, normalize overlay keys against existing env keys case-insensitively before assignment (find-and-replace the canonical-cased key). Consider an allowlist of env vars the renderer may set instead of a blocklist.

findings.title: PTY callbacks send to possibly-destroyed webContents; renderer-supplied session id used raw in channel names
findings.description: The onData/onExit closures use mainWindow?.webContents.send with no webContents.isDestroyed() guard; in the window between window.destroy() (close-ready handler at 703-707, or the 3 s force timer at 208-211) and the 'closed' event nulling mainWindow (214-220), a streaming PTY chunk throws an uncaught 'Object has been destroyed' in the main process. Separately, options.id is an arbitrary renderer string interpolated directly into channel names `pty:data:${options.id}` with no format validation — channel-namespace pollution is possible and the dynamic-channel-per-session design has no upper bound.
findings.recommendation: Guard every send with mainWindow && !mainWindow.webContents.isDestroyed(); validate ids against /^[A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,64}$/. Longer term, the multiplexed single-channel router from the flow-control fix makes this whole class of issues disappear.

findings.title: parseGitStatus miscounts common states and collides basenames; git status poll costs 4 cmd.exe spawns
findings.description: The counters only match ' M'/'M ' etc., so 'MM' (staged+modified), 'AM', renames ('R '), and copies aren't counted in modified/added, making the status bar numbers quietly wrong. fileStatuses is keyed by basename (133-137), so src/a/index.ts and src/b/index.ts overwrite each other's status. And each git:status call runs up to four sequential git processes (366-396), every one wrapped in a cmd.exe spawn on Windows (runtime-utils.ts:30-34) — expensive per poll, multiplied per session/panel that calls it (TerminalCommandBar.tsx:546, FileExplorer.tsx:204, swarm reporters).
findings.recommendation: One call: `git status --porcelain=v2 --branch` gives branch, ahead/behind, and per-file XY states in a single spawn; parse XY properly and key fileStatuses by full repo-relative path only.

findings.title: Dev cache directories accumulate forever in %TEMP%
findings.description: In dev, sessionData goes to temp/GhostShell-dev/session-<pid> (50-52). Startup only rmSync's the CURRENT pid's cache dirs (61-65); every previous dev run's session-<pid> tree is left behind, so the temp folder grows unboundedly across dev sessions with Chromium cache junk.
findings.recommendation: On startup, sweep temp/GhostShell-dev/* entries older than N days (or whose pid is no longer alive) before creating the new one.

findings.title: Every window close pays the handshake tax; global isClosing state assumes exactly one window
findings.description: The close handshake (200-212) preventDefaults every close and waits for the renderer or a 3-second timer. If the renderer is hung or mid-reload, quitting the app takes a flat 3 s with no feedback. isClosing/closeForceTimer are module-level singletons while macOS 'activate' (818-822) can create additional windows sharing that state; and updater quitAndInstall (updater.ts:120) has to fight the same preventDefault path to get the app down.
findings.recommendation: Track the handshake per-window (WeakMap window→state), shorten the timeout to ~800 ms, and skip the handshake entirely when the renderer never registered onBeforeClose or when quitting for an update (set a bypass flag before quitAndInstall).

strengths: Correct Electron security baseline where it counts most: contextIsolation:true, nodeIntegration:false, a single contextBridge.exposeInMainWorld with a typed API (electron/preload.ts:120-122, electron/main.ts:186-187) — no remote module, no raw ipcRenderer exposure.

Every preload event subscription (ptyOnData, ptyOnExit, onUpdaterStatus, onBeforeClose) returns an unsubscribe function, and the renderer actually calls them in effect cleanup (preload.ts:19-28, src/hooks/usePty.ts:1552-1574) — the listener-leak discipline is real.
window.open is denied wholesale and external URLs are protocol-allowlisted to http/https/mailto (electron/main.ts:222-227, electron/runtime-utils.ts:44-51).

The dangerous-env-var filter for PTY children (LD_PRELOAD, DYLD_*, NODE_OPTIONS, ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE — pty-manager.ts:177) shows genuine awareness of child-process injection vectors; keep it (as an allowlist).
runCommand is carefully written: settled-flag prevents double resolve/reject, timeout always cleared, stderr folded into error messages, CRLF normalized (runtime-utils.ts:60-115).
writeLockFileAtomic's tmp+rename with EPERM retry ladder (swarm-file-lock-manager.ts:53-74) is exactly the right Windows-aware atomic-write pattern — it just needs to be promoted to a shared util.

The close handshake concept (let the renderer snapshot tabs, force-destroy after a timeout — main.ts:200-212, 703-707) is the right instinct for a terminal that must persist session state; it only needs per-window state and a shorter fuse.

Packaging is done right for node-pty: asarUnpack of the native module, npmRebuild disabled in favor of N-API prebuilds, and node-pty 1.1.0 actually installed with win32-x64/arm64 prebuilds present (electron-builder.yml:12-16).
Storage and workspace keys are sanitized against path traversal and reserved names before becoming filenames (main.ts:104-111, runtime-utils.ts:37-42).

The PTY spawn-plan builder with de-duplicated (shell, cwd, conpty) combinations (pty-manager.ts:117-151) is a clean structure for a fallback chain, and the ConPTY-first rationale for keeping bracketed pastes intact for agent CLIs is well reasoned and documented.
analyses.summary: The main process is a single ~830-line setupIPC() registering ~40 flat ipcMain handlers over a per-session dynamic-channel scheme (`pty:data:${id}`), backed by a small PtyManager (node-pty 1.1.0, ConPTY-first with a winpty fallback chain), a runCommand helper that shells everything through cmd.exe, and JSON-file persistence for storage/workspaces/swarm locks. The security baseline (contextIsolation, no nodeIntegration, disposer-returning preload API) is genuinely correct, but behind the bridge sits an unscoped filesystem/exec surface with no sender validation and sandbox disabled. The core terminal data path has zero flow control or chunk coalescing — every node-pty chunk becomes its own webContents.send into a heavyweight renderer handler — and the flagship checkpoint/rollback feature can permanently delete untracked files via `git clean -fd`. A WezTerm-quality rebuild needs three structural moves: a multiplexed, backpressured PTY channel with generation-tagged events; a validated, workspace-scoped IPC router; and Job-Object-based process lifecycle plus atomic persistence shared across all writers.

The smart-input layer is a window-CustomEvent-glued trio: TerminalCommandBar (a 1,321-line god component owning path resolution, repo/package-manager detection, fuzzy scoring, and three UI modes), QuickLaunchRedesign (1,140 lines, re-exported through a one-line QuickLaunch.tsx shim), and a set of overlays (MultiLineInput, TerminalSearch, SessionTypeSelector, TerminalContextPanel) absolutely positioned inside each pane. Prompt submission has one clean funnel (terminalPromptSubmission.ts: normalize -> register history/blocks/companion -> single batched ptyWrite with provider-aware newline sequence), but MultiLineInput bypasses it entirely with its own known-buggy backslash+CR protocol. Cross-component communication happens over 15 window CustomEvents ('ghostshell:focus-command-bar' duplicated as a string literal in 3 files; 'ghostshell:refit'; 'ghostshell:open-settings'; plus 12 SHORTCUT_EVENTS: new-terminal, rename-tab, split-session, terminal-search, multiline-input, clear-terminal, clear-scrollback, scroll-to-top, scroll-to-bottom, select-all, copy-path, focus-terminal), gated by isActive flags rather than any real event bus or command registry. Windows support in QuickLaunch is demonstrably broken despite Windows 11 being the target platform.
strengths: terminalPromptSubmission.ts (C:/Users/chitu/Desktop/GhostShell-main/src/lib/terminalPromptSubmission.ts:50-98) is genuinely good: one funnel that normalizes CRLF, registers history + command block + companion entry, and batches the whole multiline payload into a single ptyWrite to guarantee ordering -- the rationale documented in usePty.ts:971-975 (chunk interleaving made Claude register phantom paste blocks) is correct, hard-won engineering and should be the ONLY submission path.

TerminalCommandBar's suggestion pipeline is factored into small pure functions (scoreSearchText, filterSuggestionItems, dedupeSuggestionItems, findPrefixSuggestion, buildPathSuggestion at TerminalCommandBar.tsx:324-453) that are trivially unit-testable -- keep them, just move them out of the component file.

The debounced live-filesystem path completion (TerminalCommandBar.tsx:794-814) correctly uses a 110ms timer plus a cancelled flag, and resolvePathSuggestions handles ~, .., ./, drive letters, and directory-only filtering for cd -- a real Warp-class feature.

onMouseDown={e => e.preventDefault()} on every suggestion/action button (TerminalCommandBar.tsx:1028, 1235, 1267; QuickLaunchRedesign.tsx:746) to keep input focus is applied consistently -- the focus model was thought about.
QuickLaunch.tsx being a one-line re-export shim means the old QuickLaunch implementation was actually deleted, not left as a dueling zombie -- rare discipline for this codebase.
shortcutEvents.ts centralizes 12 shortcut event names as constants instead of scattering string literals (the focus-command-bar event being the one exception).

Narrow zustand selectors with explanatory comments (TerminalContextPanel.tsx:49-50, TerminalPane.tsx:51-56) show deliberate re-render awareness -- e.g. selecting only currentActivity/currentDetail instead of the whole activity object to dodge spinner-frame churn.

readOnly smart-input mode in usePty (usePty.ts:1027-1055) still supports Ctrl+C SIGINT, Ctrl+Shift+C copy, Ctrl+A select-all, and routes right-click/Ctrl+V paste into the command bar via the focus event with a text payload (TerminalCommandBar.tsx:851-863) -- the interaction model for the readonly terminal is coherent.

TerminalCommandBar's history/palette mode state machine (restoreInputRef save/restore on mode toggle, exit-on-pane-deactivate at lines 871-879, 892-921) handles the annoying edge cases (toggle same mode = restore, Escape = restore, accept = discard) correctly.

findings.title: MultiLineInput submits with the backslash+CR sequence that usePty's own comment documents as buggy
findings.description: handleMultiLineSubmit (TerminalPane.tsx:270-306) writes '\\' then '\r' between lines for Claude, while usePty.ts:196-204 explicitly says: 'The old approach (\\ + CR) showed a visible backslash and caused double newlines on Windows because the PTY CR echo stacked with the CLI's own continuation newline' and uses '\x1b\r' instead -- as does terminalPromptSubmission.ts:23-26. So the app contains three multiline protocols and the one wired to the Ctrl-shift-multiline overlay is the one the codebase itself calls broken. Worse: provider defaults to 'claude' when there is no agent and no detectedProvider (line 276), so multiline text sent to a plain PowerShell session emits line + '\\' + '\r' per line -- CR submits in PowerShell, so each line of the user's 'single prompt' executes immediately with a trailing backslash appended.
findings.recommendation: Delete handleMultiLineSubmit's hand-rolled writer and call submitPromptToSession(session.id, text, session.cwd) -- it already picks '\x1b\r' vs '\n' per provider and batches into one ptyWrite. Add a third branch for provider-less plain shells (PowerShell needs no continuation at all if you paste via bracketed paste; reuse writeInjectedText's bracketed-paste path).

findings.title: MultiLineInput submissions invisible to history, command blocks, and companion log
findings.description: handleMultiLineSubmit writes straight to window.ghostshell.ptyWrite and never calls registerPromptSubmission, while the command bar path (TerminalCommandBar.tsx:932 -> terminalPromptSubmission.ts:87-98) records every prompt into historyStore, commandBlockStore, and companionStore. Multiline prompts therefore never appear in Ctrl+R history, the blocks panel, or the TerminalContextPanel conversation feed -- silent data inconsistency between two submission paths for the same user intent.
findings.recommendation: Once MultiLineInput routes through submitPromptToSession (previous finding), this fixes itself for free -- one funnel, one source of truth.

findings.title: QuickLaunch directory autocomplete is 100% broken on Windows (builds /C:/... paths, verified ENOENT)
findings.description: The autocomplete effect normalizes every typed path into '/' + segments.join('/') (lines 344-357), so 'C:\\projects\\gh' becomes parentDir '/C:/projects' and relative input against resolvedPath 'C:\\Users\\chitu' becomes '/C:/Users/chitu/...'. Verified on this machine: fs.readdirSync('/C:/Users') throws ENOENT on Windows Node. api.fsReadDir(parentDir) therefore always fails and suggestions stay empty for every Windows path -- on an app whose owner runs Windows 11. The same '/'-prefix bug exists in the renderer fallback resolveInputPath (line 144: finalPath = '/' + resolved.join('/')), and both drive-letter regexes (lines 132, 339: /^[A-Z]:[/\\]/) lack the 'i' flag so 'c:/foo' is misparsed as relative.
findings.recommendation: Delete the renderer-side path math entirely and make shellResolvePath IPC (which exists in electron/preload.ts:108) the only resolver; for autocomplete, add a shellReadDirResolved(fragment, base) IPC that does path.resolve in the main process. WezTerm-quality means the OS path semantics live in exactly one native-side module.

findings.title: QuickLaunch home-directory fallback has no Windows branch and explicitly discards Windows workspace paths
findings.description: The homeDir detector (lines 248-290) probes only /Users (macOS, with a 'pick the single non-system dir' heuristic that breaks on multi-user machines) and /home (Linux) -- there is no C:\\Users branch, and the regex at line 261 matches only /Users|/home prefixes. Meanwhile resolvedPath (line 294) contains `!/^[A-Z]:\\\\/.test(currentPath)` -- deliberately excluding Windows drive paths from the currentPath fallback. Comments like '(works after full Electron restart)' (lines 111, 253) reveal these are dev-hot-reload workarounds shipped as permanent code paths.
findings.recommendation: Trust the shellGetHomedir IPC as the single source (it exists in preload.ts:107), fetch it once at app boot into a store, delete all three filesystem-probing fallbacks, and remove the anti-Windows currentPath filter.

findings.title: SessionTypeSelector's window keydown listener fires on '1'/'2' typed into inputs still focused behind the modal
findings.description: handleKeyDown (lines 176-188) is attached to window with no focus trap, no e.target check, and no modifier check. TerminalCommandBar aggressively re-focuses its input (TerminalCommandBar.tsx:830-838), and the modal never steals focus, so keydown events from the still-focused command bar bubble to window: typing '1' both inserts '1' into the smart input AND instantly launches GhostCode (or Ctrl+1 tab-switch shortcuts double-fire). Also '1'/'2' fire even with ctrl/alt held.
findings.recommendation: Trap focus in the modal on mount (focus a container with tabIndex=-1), check !e.ctrlKey && !e.metaKey && !e.altKey and that e.target isn't an input/textarea, and preventDefault when consuming the key.

findings.title: Search highlight decorations are never cleared when the search bar closes
findings.description: TerminalSearch's cleanup lives in the effect's isOpen===false branch (lines 16-24: setQuery(''), onClear()), but TerminalPane renders it as `{searchOpen && <TerminalSearch isOpen={searchOpen} .../>}` (TerminalPane.tsx:538-548) -- the component unmounts before isOpen can ever be false, and the effect has no return cleanup, so searchAddon.clearDecorations() (useTerminal.ts:389-391) never runs. Closing search leaves stale match highlights painted in the terminal. Bonus jank: the component is double-positioned -- its own 'absolute top-1 right-2 z-30' stacks inside TerminalPane's wrapper 'absolute top-2 right-4 z-20', so offsets accumulate and the z-indexes contradict each other.
findings.recommendation: Return a cleanup function from the effect (`return () => onClear()`), delete the isOpen prop/branch entirely (mount = open), and position it in exactly one place.

findings.title: Command bar suggestion dropdown has no max-height or scrolling -- clipped and unreachable in short panes
findings.description: The dropdown (lines 1012-1086) renders up to 12 history rows at h-14 (56px) each = 672px, positioned 'absolute bottom-full' growing upward. The ancestor .terminal-pane has overflow-hidden (TerminalPane.tsx:348), so in a half-height split pane the top suggestions are clipped invisible; keyboard selection can move onto rows the user cannot see or click. There is also no scroll-into-view for the selected index.
findings.recommendation: Add max-h-[min(50vh,420px)] overflow-y-auto to the dropdown, and scrollIntoView({block:'nearest'}) on selectedIndex change -- table stakes for a command palette.

findings.title: Inline ghost-text autocomplete misaligns on scrolled input and leading whitespace
findings.description: The suffix overlay (lines 1117-1125) renders a transparent copy of `input` as a spacer plus the suffix, but never mirrors the input element's scrollLeft -- once the command is wider than the field, the real text scrolls while the overlay stays pinned, painting ghost text over the wrong characters. Independently, findPrefixSuggestion matches against input.trim() (lines 374-384) while getSuggestionSuffix slices with untrimmed input.length (lines 392-396): with input ' git', candidate 'git status' matches but the suffix comes out as 'tatus'-style off-by-N garbage.
findings.recommendation: Sync overlay scroll with input.scrollLeft in onScroll (WezTerm/Warp do exactly this), and compute the suffix from the same normalized string used for matching -- or reject suggestions when input has leading whitespace.

findings.title: TerminalCommandBar re-renders on every PTY output chunk while a command runs
findings.description: The selector `state.blocksBySession[sessionId] ?? EMPTY_COMMAND_BLOCKS` (lines 622-624) returns the fresh array commandBlockStore.appendOutput creates per output chunk (commandBlockStore.ts:142-178, blocks.map producing new references). Every chunk from e.g. 'npm run dev' re-renders the whole 1,300-line component and recomputes blockSuggestions (lines 724-731), which feeds block.output/rawOutput strings into buildBlockSuggestion and scoring -- typing latency in the bar degrades exactly when a command is streaming.
findings.recommendation: Subscribe to a stable projection (e.g. a memoized per-session list of {id, command, status, cwd} that only changes on block start/finish), or gate the block-suggestion source behind palette mode being open.

findings.title: Repo context (git status, scripts) computed once per cwd and never refreshed -- recommendations go stale
findings.description: resolveRepoContext (lines 539-612) runs gitStatus + up-to-6-level parent fsReadDir walks only when cwd changes (effect at 816-828). After the user runs 'git commit' or 'git push' through the bar, the palette still recommends 'Push branch -- N local commits ahead' and 'N changed files' from the snapshot taken at mount. With multiple smart-input panes on the same cwd, each pane redundantly repeats the identical IPC walk (no shared cache).
findings.recommendation: Move repo context into a small shared store keyed by packageRoot with a TTL, and invalidate it when a command block finishes in that cwd (commandBlockStore already knows). One fetch per repo, refreshed on activity.

findings.title: Triplicated provider/multiline logic across the submission stack
findings.description: getNativeMultilineSequence exists twice (terminalPromptSubmission.ts:23-26 and usePty.ts:196-204, the latter with the authoritative comment); detectProviderFromCommand is duplicated verbatim (terminalPromptSubmission.ts:28-48 vs usePty.ts:148-168); the 'ghostshell:focus-command-bar' event name is a string literal in three files (usePty.ts:34, TerminalCommandBar.tsx:68, TerminalPane.tsx:22) instead of living in shortcutEvents.ts; QuickLaunchRedesign re-declares the provider list (lines 55-59) and the provider-to-icon mapping three separate times (lines 418, 949, 996) instead of extending src/lib/providers.ts; and isAbsolutePath/drive-letter regexes appear in four flavors with inconsistent case sensitivity (TerminalCommandBar.tsx:88-89 case-insensitive vs QuickLaunchRedesign.tsx:132,339 uppercase-only).
findings.recommendation: Single canonical module: multiline sequence + provider detection in providers.ts (or terminalPromptSubmission.ts), provider icon/label/color as one PROVIDER_META record, event name exported from shortcutEvents.ts, and one path-predicate helper. Duplication here already diverged into a live bug (the backslash+CR path).

findings.title: Gradients in the command bar and context panel violate the project's own NO GRADIENTS rule
findings.description: TerminalCommandBar's root uses background: 'linear-gradient(180deg, ...)' (line 989) and TerminalContextPanel uses bg-[linear-gradient(180deg,rgba(10,10,10,0.96),rgba(5,5,5,0.98))] (TerminalContextPanel.tsx:73) -- both direct violations of CLAUDE.md ('NO GRADIENTS ... SOLID COLORS ONLY'), and both gradients are so subtle they read as solid anyway.
findings.recommendation: Replace both with the single solid color-mix values the rest of the Glass UI theme uses; visual delta is nil.

findings.title: TerminalCommandBar and QuickLaunchRedesign are god components (1,321 and 1,140 lines)
findings.description: TerminalCommandBar.tsx contains ~550 lines of pure logic (path resolution 455-537, repo/package-manager discovery 539-612, scoring/filtering/dedupe 324-396) plus a three-mode state machine plus 340 lines of JSX, all in one file with 15 useMemo/useEffect blocks. QuickLaunchRedesign.tsx similarly fuses path resolution, homedir probing, autocomplete, preset CRUD, agent creation orchestration (handleLaunch's 80-line session-reuse dance at 523-606), and two wizard steps. Neither has a single test, and neither can be tested as written.
findings.recommendation: Extract lib/pathCompletion.ts, lib/repoContext.ts, hooks/useCommandSuggestions.ts, and a SuggestionList component; QuickLaunch's launch orchestration belongs next to useAgent, not inside a wizard's onClick.

findings.title: Dead code and mojibake fossil: footerText computed with 'Ã‚Â·' replaceAll but never rendered; provider prop provably always undefined
findings.description: Line 978: `const footerText = footerLabel.replaceAll('Ã‚Â·', '·')` -- a double-UTF8-encoding bandage for a corrupted middle-dot -- is never used; displayFooterText (980-982) hardcodes an ASCII replacement, which also makes footerLabel's fallback string at 967 unreachable. Separately, the `provider` prop is always undefined by construction: showSmartInput requires !session.agentId && !session.detectedProvider (TerminalPane.tsx:64), which is exactly the condition making provider undefined at TerminalPane.tsx:62-63 -- so the `${provider} command line` header branch (lines 999-1001) is dead. QuickLaunch's no-sessionId branches (QuickLaunchRedesign.tsx:494-499, 591-599) are also dead: the only call site (TerminalPane.tsx:339) always passes sessionId.
findings.recommendation: Delete footerText/footerLabel's dead branches and the provider prop; make sessionId required in QuickLaunchProps and delete the else branches. Dead code that encodes a fixed encoding bug is pure confusion for the rebuild.

findings.title: 5x3 layout declares 14 sessions but renders 15 preview dots
findings.description: LAYOUTS entry `{ layout: '5x3', count: 14, cols: 5, rows: 3 }` -- LayoutDots draws cols*rows = 15 dots (lines 73-87) while the label says '14 Sessions' and launch creates 14 agents, leaving one silently empty grid cell (BentoLayout maps 13-15 -> 5x3). Either count is a typo for 15 or the preview lies.
findings.recommendation: Derive count from cols*rows in one place, or render the preview from count with the last cell dimmed.

findings.title: Invalid HTML: preset delete button nested inside a motion.button
findings.description: The saved-preset chip is a <motion.button> (line 796) containing a nested <button> for delete (lines 811-816). button-in-button is invalid HTML with undefined event/focus behavior across browsers, breaks keyboard activation of the inner control (Enter/Space on the chip can't reach it), and screen readers announce it unpredictably.
findings.recommendation: Make the chip a div with role='button' or restructure as a chip div containing two sibling buttons -- the standard pattern for card-with-delete.

findings.title: QuickLaunch StepBar and close button scroll away with content; Back vs X have contradictory semantics
findings.description: StepBar (absolute top-[60px], line 186) and the X button (absolute top-10 right-10, line 626) are absolutely positioned inside the overflow-y-auto root (lines 611-615), so on short windows they scroll out of view with the content -- the wizard loses its step indicator and escape hatch mid-scroll; content compensates with a magic pt-[110px] (line 636). Also inconsistent: X removes the session entirely (lines 619-624) while step-1 'Back' (lines 896-902) calls onLaunched leaving an empty terminal behind -- two cancel affordances, two different destructive outcomes.
findings.recommendation: Move StepBar/X outside the scroll container (sticky header row), and unify cancel semantics: both should do the same thing, decided once.

findings.title: MultiLineInput Send button covers the textarea resize grip; Escape discards text with no guard
findings.description: The Send button (absolute bottom-4 right-5, lines 110-117) sits exactly over the textarea's bottom-right corner where the native resize-y grip renders -- users can't grab the resize handle the component advertises. Escape (lines 37-41) closes and discards arbitrarily long typed prompts with zero confirmation. Focus/border styling is done by mutating e.currentTarget.style in onFocus/onBlur (lines 101-108) instead of CSS classes, and the close button has no aria-label.
findings.recommendation: Dock the Send button below the textarea (flex row footer), confirm-on-escape when value is non-empty (or stash the draft per session), use focus-visible CSS, add aria-labels.

findings.title: SessionTypeSelector: exit animations never play, 'SHIFT + CLICK Raw Terminal' hint is wrong in one of two entry points, fixed 360x480 cards clip on narrow windows, mixed-language copy
findings.description: AnimatePresence (line 191) is INSIDE the component, but both parents conditionally unmount the whole component (TerminalContainer.tsx:198, GlobalDock.tsx:353), so the carefully authored exit variants (lines 68, 198, 244, 273) are dead code. The footer advertises 'SHIFT + CLICK -> Raw Terminal' (lines 281-283) but shift-click inside the modal does nothing -- that shortcut only exists on the dock '+' button (GlobalDock.tsx:149-155) and doesn't exist at all for TerminalContainer's 'Start New Session' entry. Two fixed 360px cards + 64px gaps + divider (~900px) inside overflow-hidden (line 192) clip on windows under ~1000px wide with no wrap or scale-down. Card descriptions are Spanish ('Entorno individual potenciado por IA', lines 230, 257) in an otherwise English UI.
findings.recommendation: Hoist AnimatePresence to the parent (or drop the exit variants), make the modal actually handle shiftKey in onClick to spawn a raw terminal, use clamp()/max-w with flex-wrap for the cards, and pick one language.

findings.title: Focus-request event contract is fragile: missing sessionId focuses every pane's bar; paste injection reads DOM value racing React state
findings.description: handleFocusRequest (lines 840-869) returns early only when detail.sessionId exists AND mismatches -- an event without detail focuses every mounted command bar (last-mounted wins the focus war). The paste path splices detail.text into field.value (the raw DOM value, lines 851-863) then setInput(next): two rapid events (e.g. paste + Wispr Flow injection) read stale DOM before React flushes, silently dropping the first payload. The isActive auto-focus timer (lines 830-838, 80ms) additionally steals focus on every remount regardless of what the user is doing.
findings.recommendation: Make sessionId required in the event contract (typed helper in shortcutEvents.ts), apply text via functional setInput(prev => ...) with a caret ref, and only auto-focus when document.activeElement is body/terminal.

findings.title: Command bar a11y: no combobox semantics anywhere in the suggestion UI
findings.description: The input (line 1127) has no aria-label, no role='combobox', no aria-expanded/aria-controls; the dropdown (1012-1086) is a div of buttons with no listbox/option roles or aria-activedescendant, so arrow-key selection is invisible to assistive tech; selected state is conveyed by background color only. Same pattern in TerminalSearch (input unlabeled, TerminalSearch.tsx:58-67) and QuickLaunch's suggestion list (QuickLaunchRedesign.tsx:743-760).
findings.recommendation: Standard WAI-ARIA combobox pattern: role=combobox + aria-expanded on the input, role=listbox/option with ids on rows, aria-activedescendant tracking selectedIndex, aria-label on all icon-only buttons.

findings.title: historyStore suggestion scoring uses a timestamp-magnitude magic threshold
findings.description: getCommandSuggestions filters candidates with `if (normalizedQuery && score <= entry.timestamp / 1_000_000_000_000) continue` -- comparing a match score against epoch-milliseconds divided by 1e12 (~1.77 in 2026, slowly increasing forever). It happens to mean 'score must exceed a tiny recency epsilon' today but is an unlabeled, time-drifting heuristic feeding the command bar's primary suggestion source, and the sort at line 235 re-invokes scoreCommand O(n log n) times per keystroke instead of scoring once.
findings.recommendation: Score once into a decorated array, filter with an explicit named constant (MIN_MATCH_SCORE), and document the recency weighting -- or port the scoring to the same scoreSearchText utility the bar already has.

findings.title: Escape wipes the entire typed command with no recovery
findings.description: In normal mode, Escape with any input clears it outright (lines 1204-1215). Terminal users press Escape reflexively (vim habits, dismissing completions); a long composed command is unrecoverable -- there is no undo stack and, per the earlier finding, it also wasn't in history unless submitted.
findings.recommendation: First Escape dismisses the inline suggestion only; second Escape clears but stashes the value in restoreInputRef (the mechanism already exists for mode toggles) so ArrowUp or Escape-again restores it.

analyses.summary: PTY output flows from ConPTY through main (electron/main.ts:280 forwards every raw chunk verbatim over IPC with no coalescing) into usePty.ts, where each chunk is mutated in-place before terminal.write(): imageLabels.maskText rewrites file paths (usePty.ts:766), sanitizeReadOnlyDisplay strips prompt echoes, and enhanceTerminalOutput injects SGR color codes (usePty.ts:774, ON by default via settingsStore.ts:306). In parallel, createBatchParser regex-scans a rolling 2000-char buffer every 100ms to infer activity/sub-agents/context metrics. Every transformation is chunk-local and stateless across chunk boundaries, and every detector is a loose keyword regex — an architecture that is fundamentally unsound against a constantly-repainting TUI like Claude Code, and is the direct cause of 'text looks wrong when running Claude' artifacts.
strengths: The bracketed-paste path is genuinely well engineered: single atomic IPC write wrapped in \x1b[200~/201~ (usePty.ts:976-989), xterm's native paste handler preempted at capture phase on both termEl and the helper textarea (usePty.ts:1211-1216, 1294-1299), and pty-manager.write() hands the full payload to node-pty in one call (electron/pty-manager.ts:220-227). The comments document the real double-paste bugs this fixed — keep this design verbatim in a rebuild.

electron/pty-manager.ts spawn logic is solid: ConPTY-first with winpty fallback and preferred/fallback shell+cwd plan matrix (lines 136-151), dangerous env var filtering (LD_PRELOAD/NODE_OPTIONS/ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE, lines 176-183), and PowerShell -NoLogo/-NoProfile/-ExecutionPolicy startup args (lines 46-65).

enhanceLine's guard that skips any line containing \x1b (terminalOutputEnhancer.ts:115-118) shows correct awareness that mutating escape sequences corrupts TUIs — the right instinct applied at the wrong layer; the guard just cannot work chunk-locally.

terminalPresets.ts is clean pure data: typed provider visual profiles with runtime validation guards (isCursorStyle/isCliVisualProfile/isProvider, lines 39-53) and explicit deep-merge of search/theme overrides — directly reusable.
The image label registry concept (stable 'Image N' label per temp path, terminalImageLabels.ts) is a good UX idea with real unit tests; only its application point (raw VT stream) is wrong.

StrictMode-aware deferred PTY init to avoid double PTY creation in dev (usePty.ts:1545-1550) and the withTerminal try/catch teardown-race wrapper (usePty.ts:363-370) show real debugging of Electron+React lifecycle races.

createBatchParser has a bounded buffer, a destroy() lifecycle hooked into the effect cleanup (usePty.ts:1561), and lazy provider resolution via closure — the skeleton is fine even though the parsing inside it is not.
Vitest is wired up with some real unit tests (terminalImageLabels, terminalTextInput), which is more than most AI-generated Electron apps ship with.

findings.title: enhanceTerminalOutput injects SGR into escape sequences split across chunk boundaries, garbling Claude Code's TUI
findings.description: The enhancer is stateless per chunk, but electron/main.ts:280-281 forwards raw ConPTY reads verbatim, so escape sequences routinely split across IPC messages. If chunk N ends with a bare \x1b and chunk N+1 starts with '[2K\rReading foo.ts', the guard `line.includes('\x1b')` (line 118) passes because the ESC byte lives in the previous chunk, so enhanceLine wraps '[2K...' with '\x1b[1m\x1b[95m...'. The terminal then sees ESC followed by ESC — the first sequence aborts and '[2K' renders as literal text, producing exactly the duplicated/garbled-line artifacts reported when running Claude. Same failure for the OSC guard at line 140: a split '\x1b]0;title\x07' leaves ']0;title' in a chunk with no '\x1b]', which gets colorized and printed as literal text. This is ON by default (settingsStore.ts:306 terminalOutputEmphasis:'balanced') and applied ONLY to Claude (usePty.ts:770-774), the most repaint-heavy TUI of the three providers. Corruption is chunk-timing dependent, matching the intermittent nature of the bug.
findings.recommendation: Delete the stream-rewriting enhancer entirely. WezTerm-quality terminals never mutate the byte stream between PTY and parser. If semantic highlighting is wanted, run a real VT parser (e.g. reuse xterm.js's parser hooks: terminal.parser.registerCsiHandler / onLineFeed) or use xterm's Decoration/Marker API to overlay styles on rendered buffer lines after the fact — zero bytes injected. Any component that must inspect the stream needs a stateful tokenizer that carries partial-sequence remainder bytes across chunks.

findings.title: imageLabels.maskText rewrites raw PTY data with different-length text, desyncing TUI column math
findings.description: usePty.ts:766 runs maskText over every raw PTY chunk forever once an image is attached. Replacing a ~55-char temp path (e.g. C:\Users\...\Temp\ghostshell-img-*.png) with 7-char 'Image 1' shifts every subsequent character on that row left by ~48 columns, while Claude Code's input-box repaint computes borders, padding, and backspace counts against the REAL text length it echoed — so box borders break, erase sequences eat the wrong cells, and wrapped lines misalign. Additionally the mask is chunk-local: a path split across two IPC chunks matches neither chunk, so the raw path intermittently leaks through, and the third unquoted replace (line 32) fires on partial contexts. The registry never clears labels, and lines 28-32 compile 3 new RegExp objects per label per chunk on the hot output path.
findings.recommendation: Never rewrite PTY bytes for cosmetics. If temp image paths should read as 'Image 1', do it at the presentation layer only: register an xterm link/decoration provider that matches the path in the rendered buffer and overlays a label, or mask only in GhostShell-owned surfaces (command blocks, companion chat, history) which already receive maskedData separately. Precompile the regexes once per label and cache them if masking is kept anywhere.

findings.title: Regex-triggered auto-confirm blindly types 'y\r' into agent PTYs
findings.description: For any agent session, every raw output chunk is tested against CLAUDE_AUTO_CONFIRM_PATTERNS (usePty.ts:48-58) — loose patterns like /\(y\)es.*\(n\)o/i, /\? \(y\/N\)/, /Continue\?.*\(y\/n\)/i — and on match GhostShell writes 'y\r' to the PTY 150ms later (lines 869-882) with no setting, no user visibility, and no confirmation. If Claude merely PRINTS text containing '(y/n)' (documentation, code, a script it is reading), GhostShell silently injects 'y' + Enter into the CLI's input box. Worse, /\? \(y\/N\)/ auto-answers YES to prompts whose safe default is NO — this silently auto-approves permission prompts, defeating the entire permission model of Claude Code from a regex false positive on unstructured output.
findings.recommendation: Remove blind auto-confirm. If auto-approval is a desired feature, gate it behind an explicit per-agent opt-in setting, use the CLI's own sanctioned mechanism (--dangerously-skip-permissions / --approval-mode which the app already supports in providers.ts), and never synthesize keystrokes from regex matches on the output stream.

findings.title: Keyword-based line classification recolors ordinary prose; nested wraps half-paint lines
findings.description: detectHighlightKind (lines 64-74) turns any line containing 'error|failed|not found|denied' bold-red (line 70) — so Claude saying 'this handles the error case' renders as an error. CONTEXT_LINE_VALUE_PATTERN (line 39) classifies any line containing '$5', '12 tokens' or 'Turn 3' as a context line and paints it bold cyan. ACTION_PATTERN (line 28) recolors bare English words like 'Read', 'Running', 'Done' mid-prose. Compounding it, enhanceInlineTokens wraps tokens with COLOR...RESET first, then wrapImportantLine (line 130) wraps the WHOLE already-mutated line — the inner \x1b[0m terminates the outer style, so in 'vivid' mode the line background dies at the first inner token, leaving half-painted highlight bars. Finally, the guard at line 141 only skips chunks with \r AND no \n; a bare \r inside a line that also contains \r\n (normal on ConPTY) gets wrapped as one styled unit, so spinner overwrite frames bleed color. Also line 100's ternary has identical branches (dead code).
findings.recommendation: If any highlighting survives the rebuild, classify on the rendered buffer line (xterm buffer API) not the stream, require anchored/structured markers (e.g. Claude Code's '⏺ ' tool bullets) instead of bare English words, and apply styles via decorations so app-emitted SGR state is never clobbered by injected resets.

findings.title: createBatchParser re-parses its 200-char tail and TUI repaints re-feed identical text, duplicating events and sub-agents
findings.description: After each 100ms parse, the buffer keeps its last 200 chars 'for context overlap' (line 872), so any match sitting in that tail is re-detected on every subsequent tick until 200 new chars push it out — with a slow spinner trickle that's ~20 duplicate parses. Independently, Claude Code's full-screen repaints re-transmit the same tool-call text many times per second, and each retransmission is a fresh match. Consumers barely defend against this: sub-agent spawns dedupe only within SUBAGENT_SPAWN_DEDUPE_MS=1200ms (usePty.ts:419), so a Task line visible on screen longer than 1.2s creates phantom duplicate sub-agents; addEvent/addFileTouch/companion activity events (usePty.ts:639-648) have no dedupe at all, spamming the activity feed; every re-match bumps lastWorkingPatternTime, distorting idle detection. The BUFFER_MAX slice at lines 858-859 can also cut an escape sequence in half, leaving '[0;35m'-style fragments that stripAnsi can no longer remove.
findings.recommendation: Parse line-oriented, not window-oriented: keep a proper line accumulator, parse each COMPLETE line exactly once, and drop consumed lines. Dedupe semantically (hash of tool+args) rather than by time window. Better: get activity from structured sources — Claude Code hooks or a stream-json sidecar process — instead of scraping the human-facing TUI.

findings.title: stripAnsi misses DEC private modes and ST-terminated OSC, leaking control bytes into parsed text and Companion chat
findings.description: ANSI_STRIP = /\x1b\[[0-9;]*[a-zA-Z]|\x1b\].*?\x07|\x1b\(B/g cannot match CSI sequences with a private-parameter byte: '\x1b[?25l' (cursor hide), '\x1b[?2026h' (synchronized output), '\x1b[?1049h' (alt screen) — all emitted constantly by Claude Code — because [0-9;]* cannot consume '?'. It also only matches BEL-terminated OSC, not ST-terminated ('\x1b]0;title\x1b\\'), which ConPTY/Windows emits. Result: 'stripped' text still contains raw ESC bytes and OSC payloads (window titles include cwd paths, which can trigger the loose path-capturing regexes downstream), and accumulateCompanionOutput (usePty.ts:578-588) pipes this same 'stripped' text into the Companion chat, where '[?25l'-style fragments render as visible garbage.
findings.recommendation: Use a complete, battle-tested stripper (the 'ansi-regex' pattern covers CSI private modes, OSC with BEL/ST, DCS) or a real VT tokenizer, and add a unit test with actual Claude Code output captures containing ?25l/?2026h/OSC-ST.

findings.title: 'Formal' tool-call regexes target an output format Claude Code doesn't print, while ALT fallbacks fire on arbitrary prose
findings.description: TOOL_READ = /\bRead\s*\(\s*file_path:\s*\"([^\"]+)\"/ (and Write/Edit/Bash/Glob/Grep variants, lines 8-16) expect literally 'Read(file_path: "...")'. Claude Code's TUI renders tool calls as '⏺ Read(src/foo.ts)' without key:"value" syntax, so these primary patterns essentially never match real output (unverified against every CLI version, but consistent with current Claude Code rendering) — file-touch tracking silently doesn't work. Detection then falls to the ALT patterns, which have no anchoring: TOOL_READ_ALT /(?:📖|Reading)\s+([^\s\n]+)/ turns the sentence 'Reading more about X' into a fileTouch on path 'more'; CODEX_SHELL_ALT /(?:Running|Executing|Ran)(?: command)?:?\s+`?([^`\n]+)`?/i has no \b, so 'gran torino' matches 'ran' and records running_bash 'torino'; GEMINI_READ_ALT matches the bare word 'Read' anywhere. The activity/file-history features are thus fed a mix of nothing (real tool calls) and garbage (prose).
findings.recommendation: Capture real fixtures from each CLI version and write regressions against them, or abandon TUI scraping: Claude Code exposes hooks and stream-json output; run a headless sidecar for telemetry and let the visible PTY be display-only. At minimum anchor ALT patterns to line starts with the CLI's actual bullet glyphs (⏺, ✦) and add \b boundaries.

findings.title: Context metrics regexes ingest '$1' and 'N tokens' from arbitrary output as cost/token telemetry
findings.description: COST_PATTERN = /\$(\d+(?:\.\d+)?)/ matches awk/bash positional params: any script output containing '$1' sets costEstimate=1 (extractContextUpdate, lines 94-129). TOKENS_PATTERN /(\d+...[kKmM]?)\s*tokens?/i matches prose like 'uses 5 tokens', overwriting the real token estimate with 5. These false updates flow to updateContextMetrics and emit 'Context: ...' system messages in Companion chat (usePty.ts:659-685), so the context gauge visibly jumps around while agents merely print code. The enhancer shares the same pattern (terminalOutputEnhancer.ts:30) and recolors '$1' in scripts as if it were spend.
findings.recommendation: Only accept context/cost metrics from the CLI's dedicated statusline region (anchor to the known statusline format/row) or from structured telemetry (hooks/stream-json). Require multiple co-occurring fields (e.g. '% context' AND 'tokens' on the same line) before trusting a match.

findings.title: Shipped test suite fails: terminalTextInput test asserts behavior the implementation deliberately removed
findings.description: Verified by running `npx vitest run src/lib/__tests__/terminalTextInput.test.ts`: 1 failed / 2 passed. The test expects shouldCaptureStructuredTextInsertion('insertFromPaste'|'insertReplacementText'|'insertFromDrop', ...) === true, but terminalTextInput.ts:22-26 only returns true for multi-char 'insertText' — the implementation comment even says 'We deliberately do NOT intercept insertFromPaste'. The behavior change was correct; the test was never updated, meaning `npm test` has been red and nobody runs it. There are also zero tests for the two most dangerous modules in this area (terminalOutputEnhancer, claude-output-parser).
findings.recommendation: Fix the stale assertions, wire vitest into CI so a red suite blocks merges, and add chunk-boundary fuzz tests for any stream transformation (split every fixture at each byte offset and assert output equivalence — the standard way terminal emulators test their parsers).

findings.title: Multi-line prompts sent to plain shells use Claude's ESC+CR sequence, wiping lines in PSReadLine
findings.description: getPromptProvider falls back to 'claude' for sessions with no agent and no detectedProvider (line 20) — i.e. a plain PowerShell tab. writePrompt (lines 50-62) then joins multi-line commands with getNativeMultilineSequence('claude') = '\x1b\r' (line 24). In PSReadLine, a bare ESC clears the current input line, so pasting a multi-line command via the command bar / history panel / CommandBlocksPanel into a normal shell destroys all lines except the last. Callers confirmed: TerminalCommandBar.tsx:932, HistoryPanel.tsx:29, SettingsModal.tsx:135, CommandBlocksPanel.tsx:146 can all target provider-less sessions.
findings.recommendation: Only use provider-specific multiline sequences when a provider is POSITIVELY identified; for plain shells, join with '\n' or send lines as separate writes, or use bracketed paste (shells treat bracketed multi-line paste correctly). Make the fallback explicit ('shell'), not 'claude'.

findings.title: TOOL_TASK matches bare 'Task (' anywhere, spawning phantom sub-agents
findings.description: TOOL_TASK = /\bTask\s*\(\s*(?:description:\s*\"([^\"]*)\")?/ — the entire argument group is optional, so the regex matches any occurrence of 'Task(' or 'Task (': C#/Java code output (`new Task(...)`) , progress text ('Task (2 of 5)'), or Claude discussing the Task tool. Each match pushes a sub_agent result with description 'Running task' (lines 164-180), creating fake sub-agent cards in the activity UI. SUBAGENT_INLINE (line 50) similarly fires whenever the word 'sub-agent' appears in prose — e.g. when Claude audits code that mentions subagents.
findings.recommendation: Require the full structured signature (non-optional description/subagent_type groups) or anchor to the CLI's actual tool-call rendering; treat prose mentions as non-events.

findings.title: PERMISSION and Gemini 'thinking' detectors match static UI text and prose, wedging activity state
findings.description: PERMISSION_PATTERN = /Allow|Deny|approve|permission/i (line 38) — any prose containing 'allowed'/'approval'/'permission' flips activity to 'permission', showing a false 'waiting for permission' state. GEMINI_THINKING = /✦|Thinking/ (line 406): '✦' is Gemini CLI's static prompt glyph rendered while IDLE, so every repaint of the idle prompt registers as 'thinking', continuously bumping lastWorkingPatternTime (usePty.ts:624) and fighting the 8s idle detector — Gemini agents can appear perpetually 'working'. The file's own comment at usePty.ts:78-79 warns that Gemini 'uses decorative sparkle... liberally', yet the parser still keys on it.
findings.recommendation: Detect permission prompts by their exact rendered structure (options list + question mark on adjacent lines), and drop glyph-based thinking detection in favor of spinner-frame CHANGES over time (frame N != frame N-1) or structured telemetry.

findings.title: Duplicated logic across usePty and lib modules invites drift
findings.description: Three functions exist as byte-identical copies: detectProviderFromCommand (usePty.ts:148-168 vs terminalPromptSubmission.ts:28-48), getNativeMultilineSequence (usePty.ts:196-204 vs terminalPromptSubmission.ts:23-26), and escapeRegExp/escapeRegex (terminalImageLabels.ts:1-3 vs usePty.ts:249-251). CLAUDE_WORKING_PATTERNS also contains six single-braille-char regexes (usePty.ts:62-67) fully subsumed by the combined pattern on line 68, duplicated again for Gemini (93-94) and Codex (118-119). If the Claude multiline sequence ever changes, one copy will be updated and the other won't — exactly the class of bug that produced the current '\x1b\r vs \\+CR' archaeology in the comments.
findings.recommendation: Extract a single provider-behavior module (multiline sequence, prompt patterns, detection) consumed by both usePty and terminalPromptSubmission; delete the redundant spinner regexes.

findings.title: buildClaudeCommand shell escaping is wrong for PowerShell and injectable
findings.description: The launch command is typed into the interactive shell (PowerShell by default on Windows). buildClaudeCommand escapes only double quotes with backslashes: config.systemPrompt.replace(/\"/g, '\\\"') (line 137). PowerShell does not use backslash escaping — embedded \" breaks the argument, `$` variables interpolate, backticks escape, and a newline in the system prompt truncates the whole command line. A system prompt containing '"; Remove-Item ...' would execute in the user's shell. customFlags (lines 149-152) are joined completely unescaped. Same weakness for gemini/codex builders.
findings.recommendation: Stop building shell strings: pass args via node-pty spawn argv (launch the CLI directly as the PTY process with an args array), or if typing into a shell is kept, use provider-agnostic safe quoting per target shell (PowerShell single-quote doubling) and reject/encode newlines.

findings.title: sanitizeReadOnlyDisplay deletes prompt-looking bytes from raw ANSI chunks in read-only panes
findings.description: In readOnly mode every chunk is edited by two regexes: an echo-stripper built from the last submitted command (lines 447-456) and a trailing-prompt stripper (lines 458-461). Both operate on raw chunks that still contain escape sequences interleaved with the prompt text, so matches are unreliable (SGR between 'PS' and path defeats the pattern) and, when they do match, they remove text bytes while leaving the surrounding cursor-movement/SGR sequences intact — shifting subsequent output and producing intermittent misalignment in the read-only mirror pane. The generic trailing '>\s*$' alternative (line 459) can also eat a legitimate '>' that ends a chunk mid-stream (e.g. HTML/diff output split at a chunk boundary).
findings.recommendation: Don't clean the stream for read-only panes. Render everything and hide prompt rows at the presentation layer using xterm buffer markers / OSC 133 shell-integration prompt marking, which identifies prompt regions robustly.

findings.title: contextMetrics reports 0% for unknown state and known window is hardcoded stale
findings.description: getContextUsagePercentage returns 0 when tokenEstimate/turnCount/costEstimate are all 0 (lines 18-20), conflating 'no data yet' with 'genuinely 0% used'; combined with getKnownContextWindow hardcoding 200000 for Claude and 0 for gemini/codex (providers.ts:249-252), the gauge shows fabricated precision for Claude and nothing for others. Given the upstream extractor's false positives (finding above), the whole metric chain is estimate-on-estimate.
findings.recommendation: Return null for unknown, render an explicit 'no data' state, and source the real context window from the CLI (statusline or structured output) rather than a hardcoded constant.

findings.title: Dead code in the enhancer and unreachable provider branches
findings.description: ANSI_PATTERN (line 27) is declared and never used (the comment at 115-117 explains it was superseded). Line 100's ternary has identical branches ('vivid' and not both yield BOLD+INFO). usePty.ts:770 hard-bypasses the enhancer for gemini and codex, making PROVIDER_ACCENTS.gemini/.codex, GEMINI_BG, CODEX_BG, getProviderBackground's non-claude branches, and the codex '>' prompt special-case (line 126) unreachable in production.
findings.recommendation: Delete the dead constants and branches, or if gemini/codex enhancement is intended, remove the bypass — but per the critical findings, the correct move is deleting the module.

findings.title: Hardcoded speculative model catalogs and loose model-discovery regexes
findings.description: CLAUDE_MODELS/GEMINI_MODELS/CODEX_MODELS (lines 13-32) hardcode model IDs labeled 'Latest Known' — a rot-by-design pattern that also drives getDefaultModel (line 90). parseDiscoveredModels' Gemini regex (line 291) includes the alternation '(?:pro|flash|flash-lite)\b', so any CLI output line containing the bare word 'pro' or 'flash' becomes a bogus model entry in Settings. detectBadge (line 358) maps any line containing 'fast' to a badge, compounding the noise.
findings.recommendation: Treat CLI-discovered models as the only source of truth with the hardcoded list as clearly-labeled last-resort fallback; require full model-ID shape (e.g. ^gemini-\d) for discovery matches.

findings.title: Per-chunk regex compilation and window-global output stash on the hot output path
findings.description: maskText constructs 3 RegExp objects per registered label on EVERY PTY chunk (lines 28-32) — during heavy Claude streaming that is thousands of avoidable compiles per second. Separately, usePty.ts:744/813 stashes the rolling 50KB export buffer on window as `__ghostshell_output_<sessionId>` — an untyped global side-channel (cleaned at teardown, line 1567, but invisible to tooling and easy to leak if teardown is skipped).
findings.recommendation: Cache compiled regexes in the registry keyed by path; replace the window stash with a proper store or a ref owned by the session object.

analyses.summary: GhostShell's visual layer is a three-way collision of styling systems: CSS custom properties (--ghost-*) mapped into Tailwind tokens, ~275 hardcoded #38bdf8 hexes plus assorted literal colors sprinkled across 40 component files, and heavy inline style={{}} objects with color-mix() recomputed per render. A well-designed theme engine (16 full themes with ANSI palettes, RGB-triplet alpha support) exists but is undermined because only 2 of 12 tokens support opacity modifiers — leaving 368 Tailwind classes that compile to nothing — and because entire surfaces (titlebar, settings modal, Electron window background) ignore it. The terminal rendering pipeline (xterm 5.5 + WebGL + fit) is genuinely careful, but the chrome around it suffers gradient/glow style-guide violations, an unmanaged z-index arms race (10 → 99999), clipped context menus, dead components (TerminalTabs, LaunchScreen, FloatingSidePanel) and a broken font pipeline (Manrope declared but never loaded, JetBrains Mono bold 700 missing, no Nerd Font fallback, CDN-only fonts in a desktop app).
strengths: useTerminal.ts is the best file in this area: scroll-position-preserving safeFit (src/hooks/useTerminal.ts:60-87), WebGL context-loss fallback with renderer downgrade (113-133), debounced ResizeObserver fits, and dispose-race guards via refs (222, 305). This is WezTerm-mindset code and should survive any rebuild.

Per-provider terminal identity in src/lib/terminalPresets.ts (cursor style, selection color, search decorations, ANSI overrides per Claude/Gemini/Codex, with executive/focus/minimal profiles) is a distinctive, well-typed system with runtime validation guards (isCursorStyle/isProvider) — keep the concept.

The theme architecture itself is sound: CSS vars + RGB triplets for alpha-capable tokens, applyTheme() keeping them in sync (src/lib/themes.ts:632-653), and 16 complete themes each with a full 16-color ANSI palette — rare thoroughness.

Terminals stay mounted (visibility toggling, not unmount) under dashboard mode to keep PTYs alive (src/components/layout/AppLayout.tsx:291-295), and TerminalContainer.tsx:115-123 uses a stable wrapper key to survive workspace-id promotion without disposing xterm — both documented with honest comments explaining the bug they prevent.

Glass UI recipes are centralized in globals.css (ghost-section-card, ghost-floating-panel, sidebar-panel) using solid translucent rgba + backdrop-blur exactly as the style guide demands; only 3 gradient offenders exist in the whole app, so compliance discipline was mostly real.
Scrollbar thumbs tinted through the theme via color-mix(var(--ghost-accent-3)...) (src/styles/globals.css:72-82) — a nice touch that follows theme switches.
The drop-target overlay implemented as a data-attribute-driven CSS ::after (src/styles/terminal.css:83-104) keeps drag-over visuals out of React render, which is the right pattern.

Accessibility touches exist where you don't expect them: aria-pressed on view toggles (TerminalTabs.tsx:294), role=switch on Toggle, aria-hidden on inert workspace layers (TerminalContainer.tsx:126), focus-visible rings in LaunchScreen.

findings.title: 368 Tailwind opacity-modifier classes compile to NOTHING — app-wide typography hierarchy is silently broken
findings.description: Only ghost.text and ghost.accent use the rgb(var(...) / <alpha-value>) form; every other ghost token is a raw var() string. Tailwind therefore drops any opacity modifier on them entirely — verified by compiling with the project's own Tailwind 3.4: text-ghost-text-dim/40, border-ghost-border/70, bg-ghost-border/50, bg-ghost-surface/60 all produce zero CSS output. A grep counts 368 occurrences (86x text-ghost-text-dim/40, 64x /30, 53x /60, 41x /50, plus bg-ghost-error/10, bg-ghost-sidebar/50, etc.). All that text silently inherits the parent color (usually full-white --ghost-text), so the intended dim/secondary text hierarchy does not exist wherever these classes are used. Concrete example: ResizeHandle (src/components/common/ResizeHandle.tsx:45-47) styles itself entirely with bg-ghost-border/40 and bg-ghost-text-dim/20 — both dropped — so the resize grip renders fully invisible.
findings.recommendation: Store every theme token as an RGB triplet (--ghost-border-rgb: 255 255 255) and map ALL Tailwind ghost colors through rgb(var(--x-rgb) / <alpha-value>), as the config comment already does for text/accent. Then add a CI check (eslint-plugin-tailwindcss or `tailwindcss --content src | diff` against a class inventory) so a class that generates no CSS fails the build. In a rebuild, generate the Tailwind theme programmatically from themes.ts so the two systems cannot drift.

findings.title: Invalid white/black opacity steps are dropped, and border-white/8 elements fall back to preflight's LIGHT GRAY #e5e7eb borders
findings.description: Tailwind's default opacity scale only has multiples of 5. Verified by compilation: border-white/8, bg-white/3, bg-white/4, border-white/6, border-white/12, bg-black/22, bg-black/28, text-white/16/18/22/24/34/42/58/72/92 generate no CSS. Worse, Tailwind preflight sets `border-color: #e5e7eb` on all elements (verified in the compiled base layer), so every `border-b border-white/8` (TerminalContextPanel.tsx:73, 74, 99, 114, 136, 148, 152, 156, 218, 255) renders a 1px LIGHT GRAY line in the dark UI instead of a 8% white hairline. Same bug in MarkdownPreview.tsx:270/286/291, StructuredDataPreview.tsx:99/217, FilePreview.tsx:128, SwarmDirectoryStep.tsx:55, and TerminalCommandBar.tsx:993/1003/1004/1031/1081/1123/1228/1237/1305 (dropped text opacities).
findings.recommendation: Sweep-replace all non-multiple-of-5 opacity suffixes with bracketed arbitrary values (border-white/[0.08], text-white/[0.24]) or round to the nearest valid step. In the rebuild, ban raw white/N in favor of 3-4 named hairline tokens (border-subtle, border-strong) defined once, and set a preflight override `* { border-color: var(--ghost-border) }` so a missed class fails dark instead of light.

findings.title: Workspace tab right-click menu is clipped to invisibility by the titlebar's overflow-hidden
findings.description: GlobalDock's root is `relative ... h-11 ... overflow-hidden` (line 218) and ContextMenu renders INSIDE it (lines 220-226) as `absolute` (ContextMenu.tsx:33-34) positioned with viewport clientX/clientY. A right-click on a tab lands at y≈15-35px inside a 44px-tall clipped container, and the ~300px-tall menu (9 colors + Default + Rename) is cut off after a few pixels — the tab color/rename context menu is effectively unusable. ContextMenu also uses `absolute` (not `fixed`) with viewport coordinates, so it is only correct by accident when its nearest positioned ancestor happens to start at (0,0).
findings.recommendation: Render ContextMenu through createPortal(document.body) with position:fixed and viewport clamping (flip when within menu-height of the bottom edge), like the FileList dropdown already does implicitly with z-[999]. A WezTerm-quality rebuild should have exactly one PopoverLayer component handling portal + clamp + Escape/outside-click for every menu in the app.

findings.title: Style-guide violations: 3 CSS gradients and a colored glow shadow, in an app whose own comments say 'no gradients, no glows'
findings.description: Direct CLAUDE.md violations found by exhaustive grep: (1) TerminalCommandBar.tsx:989 — linear-gradient(180deg, ...) background on the smart command bar; (2) TerminalContextPanel.tsx:73 — bg-[linear-gradient(180deg,rgba(10,10,10,0.96),rgba(5,5,5,0.98))]; (3) FilePreview.tsx:430 — a radial-gradient AND a linear-gradient stacked in one arbitrary class. Glow: ContextGauge.tsx:49 uses boxShadow `0 0 6px ${statusColor}40` — a colored blur glow on the context bar. Additionally globals.css:115 declares 'no pulsing' yet animate-ping/animate-pulse appear in ~20 components (TerminalPane.tsx:383, SwarmHeader.tsx:65, SwarmStatusTimeline.tsx:104, ShortcutsTab.tsx:295, etc.). Ironically several swarm files carry header comments boasting 'Glass UI, no gradients, no glows' while sibling components violate it.
findings.recommendation: Replace the two panel gradients with the solid translucent + backdrop-blur recipe already used everywhere else (the gradient endpoints differ by ~2% luminance — nobody will see the difference). FilePreview checkerboard should be a solid rgba surface. ContextGauge: drop the boxShadow, the solid statusColor fill is enough. Decide once whether pulse animations are allowed and encode it as a lint rule (no animate-ping/animate-pulse) instead of a comment.

findings.title: Font pipeline is broken: UI font never loaded, terminal bold is faux, fonts come from a CDN, no Nerd Font fallback
findings.description: index.html loads Inter + JetBrains Mono (weights 300-600 only) from Google Fonts, but the UI font stack is 'Manrope, Segoe UI Variable Text, ...' (globals.css:47, tailwind.config.js:27) — Manrope is NEVER loaded and Inter is loaded but never referenced, so the entire UI silently renders in Segoe UI and the Inter download is wasted. xterm is configured with fontWeightBold '700' (useTerminal.ts:163) but JetBrains Mono 700 is not in the CDN request, so all bold terminal text is browser-synthesized faux bold (wrong metrics, blurry under WebGL). Being CDN-only, an offline machine (a terminal app's normal habitat) falls back to Cascadia Code/Consolas with different cell metrics. The mono stack has no Nerd Font / Symbols fallback, so the powerline/icon glyphs that Claude Code, Gemini CLI and Codex CLI TUIs emit render as tofu. No ligature support (no addon, and WebGL renderer needs one). CSP even whitelists r2cdn.perplexity.ai (index.html:6) — a leftover from wherever this template was copied.
