findings.recommendation: Bundle fonts locally (@fontsource/manrope + @fontsource-variable/jetbrains-mono incl. 700, plus 'Symbols Nerd Font Mono' as the last mono fallback before 'monospace'), delete the Google Fonts links and the perplexity CSP entry, and set xterm fontFamily to '"JetBrains Mono", "Symbols Nerd Font Mono", Consolas, monospace'. That single change is the biggest visual-quality jump available toward WezTerm-level text rendering.

findings.title: SwarmViewToggle floats over the window controls — can cover the only Close button of the frameless window
findings.description: The toggle is `fixed right-3 z-[60]` with style top:6 (lines 16-17), i.e. it sits inside the 44px titlebar area at the right edge — exactly where GlobalDock renders Settings/Minimize/Maximize/Close (GlobalDock.tsx:310-351, titlebar z-20). Because the window is frame:false (electron/main.ts:179), those HTML buttons are the ONLY window controls; whenever a swarm is active the ~200px-wide toggle overlaps or fully covers them, and being z-[60] > z-20 it wins every click.
findings.recommendation: Reserve space in the titlebar layout for mode toggles instead of a fixed overlay — render SwarmViewToggle as a child of GlobalDock between the tab strip and the window controls (titlebar-no-drag). Never allow position:fixed elements into the titlebar band in a frameless window.

findings.title: Hardcoded colors defeat the 16-theme system: 275x #38bdf8 in components, purple Electron background, opaque hex titlebar and settings modal
findings.description: Three competing color systems coexist. Hardcoded hex in TSX: 275 occurrences of #38bdf8 across 40 files (plus 60x #ef4444, 55x #f59e0b, 17x #64748b...). The titlebar is bg-[#080c14] (GlobalDock.tsx:218), the settings modal background is '#0c1020' (SettingsModal.tsx:311), tab fallback color '#4094e0' (GlobalDock.tsx:49) isn't even in TAB_COLORS, and AgentHUD is bg-[#0a0f1a]/95 (AgentHUD.tsx:45). Meanwhile the BrowserWindow backgroundColor is '#1a1025' — PURPLE (electron/main.ts:181) — matching no theme (default qubria-dark bg is #0f1729, :root fallback #050912), so Windows paints purple during startup and while resizing faster than the compositor. Selecting Redline/Amber CRT/Forge Ops still shows a sky-blue logo, sky accents, a navy titlebar and a navy settings modal; the theme picker only really restyles the terminal canvas and some panels.
findings.recommendation: One rule for the rebuild: components may only reference var(--ghost-*) tokens or Tailwind ghost-* utilities; add a lint ban on hex literals in src/components. Set BrowserWindow backgroundColor from the persisted theme's bg (read settings in main before createWindow) and update it on theme change via IPC so resize exposure matches the UI.

findings.title: ~640 lines of dead visual components: TerminalTabs, LaunchScreen, FloatingSidePanel — plus duplicated tab logic in two live/dead copies
findings.description: TerminalTabs.tsx (366 lines) is imported nowhere; it near-duplicates GlobalDock's tab strip (its own Logo svg, its own getAutoColor hash, its own TAB_COLORS palette — 7 Spanish-labeled colors vs GlobalDock's 9 English ones, its own rename/context-menu logic). LaunchScreen.tsx (235 lines) is imported by App.tsx:4 which also declares launchMode state (App.tsx:15) — but neither is ever rendered/used; it even hardcodes 'v1.7.0' (LaunchScreen.tsx:220) while package.json says 2.2.0. FloatingSidePanel.tsx is unused and carries 7 unused imports. QuickLaunch.tsx is a 1-line re-export of QuickLaunchRedesign — the 'Redesign' suffix leaked into the permanent API.
findings.recommendation: Delete TerminalTabs.tsx, LaunchScreen.tsx, FloatingSidePanel.tsx, and App.tsx's dead launchMode/AnimatePresence imports; rename QuickLaunchRedesign back to QuickLaunch. Turn on TS noUnusedLocals + eslint no-unused-vars and knip/ts-prune in CI so an AI (or human) can't leave parallel implementations rotting.

findings.title: globals.css is ~35% dead: entire dock-*, ql-*, glass-panel and shortcut-key blocks style components that no longer exist
findings.description: Verified by grep across all src: .dock-bar/.dock-git-pill/.dock-new-btn/.dock-icon-btn (globals.css:317-355), .ql-root/.ql-launch-btn/.ql-specialist-card/.ql-templates-scroll (363-414), .ghost-glass-panel/.ghost-glass-panel-strong (145-159), .ghost-shortcut-key/.ghost-shortcut-key-muted (190-216), .sidebar-transition (110-113), .resize-handle (287-301) are referenced by ZERO components — GlobalDock and QuickLaunch were rewritten with inline Tailwind and the old CSS was never removed. terminal.css has the same rot: .terminal-container (49-55) is unused and `.terminal-pane .xterm { flex: 1 }` (64-66) is a no-op because the xterm mount is `absolute inset-0` (TerminalPane.tsx:536), not a flex child. The .ghost-app-shell::before pseudo-element (131-138) paints a transparent overlay — pure dead weight that still forces `> * { z-index: 1 }` stacking contexts (140-143).
findings.recommendation: Delete every verified-dead block and the ::before overlay. In the rebuild, prefer Tailwind @layer components for shared recipes so unused ones are purged automatically by the content scanner, and keep hand-written CSS files down to xterm integration only.

findings.title: Class 'no-scrollbar' is used but never defined — overflowing tab strip grows a scrollbar inside the 44px titlebar
findings.description: GlobalDock.tsx:236, TerminalTabs.tsx:194 and SwarmDelegationTree.tsx:179 use `overflow-x-auto no-scrollbar`, but globals.css only defines `.scrollbar-hide` (globals.css:6-12) and Tailwind has no built-in no-scrollbar. Verified by compilation: the class emits nothing. With enough tabs open, a styled 7px horizontal scrollbar renders inside the h-11 titlebar, compressing tab content and colliding with the drag region.
findings.recommendation: Rename usages to the existing .scrollbar-hide (or alias no-scrollbar to it in the utilities layer). Longer term, replace hidden-scroll tab strips with proper overflow affordances (chevron scroll buttons or tab shrinking) — hiding the scrollbar without an alternative is a discoverability dead end anyway.

findings.title: scale-85 is not a Tailwind class — activity icon 'scaled' header chip renders at full size
findings.description: The pane header wraps ActivityIcon in `shrink-0 scale-85 origin-left`. Tailwind's scale scale is 0/50/75/90/95/100/105/110/125/150; scale-85 compiles to nothing (verified by compilation with the project config). The icon renders unscaled, and origin-left is applied for a transform that never exists.
findings.recommendation: Use scale-[0.85] or size the icon via its `size` prop instead of a transform (transforms on text produce blurry sub-pixel rendering; the component already accepts size="xs").

findings.title: Theme startup flicker: :root fallbacks disagree with the default theme and applyTheme runs post-first-paint
findings.description: initTheme() is called in a useEffect (App.tsx:17-19), i.e. after first paint, and :root hardcodes bg #050912 / accent #38bdf8 (globals.css:16-24) while the default persisted theme qubria-dark is bg #0f1729 / accent #6366f1 (themes.ts:8,14). Every launch first paints the fallback palette, then swaps — visible background/accent color-pop, compounded by the purple Electron backgroundColor behind it (see separate finding). Note also that the DEFAULT theme's accent #6366f1 (indigo) contradicts the project style guide's mandated #38bdf8 accent.
findings.recommendation: Apply the persisted theme synchronously before ReactDOM.render (read localStorage in main.tsx, call applyTheme), keep :root values identical to the actual default theme, and reconcile the default theme's accent with the style guide (#38bdf8).

findings.title: Glass UI is internally inconsistent: applyTheme overwrites --ghost-surface with opaque hexes, making backdrop-blur panels opaque per-theme
findings.description: :root defines --ghost-surface as translucent rgba(255,255,255,0.03) (globals.css:17) per the Glass UI spec, but every theme's colors.surface is an opaque hex (#1e293b, #1e1e1e, #182444...) and applyTheme writes it straight into the var (themes.ts:636). Any component using bg-ghost-surface or var(--ghost-surface) + backdrop-blur silently loses its glass effect after theme application — the blur has nothing to show through — while components hardcoding rgba(255,255,255,0.03) stay glassy. Two different materials for the 'same' token. Meanwhile whole-screen backdrop-filter blur(24px)+ overlays (SessionTypeSelector.tsx:202, SwarmWizard.tsx:1538 backdrop-blur-3xl over 95-97% opaque backgrounds) burn GPU for an effect that is imperceptible behind near-opaque fills.
findings.recommendation: Split the token: --ghost-surface-solid (opaque, for xterm-adjacent surfaces that must not blend) and --ghost-surface-glass (translucent, always rgba). Cap overlay blur at blur-md and drop blur entirely when the overlay is >90% opaque — solid rgba(bg, 0.97) alone reads identically and composites far cheaper on Windows.

findings.title: z-index arms race with no scale: 10/20/30/50/60/100/999/9999/99999, with real stacking conflicts
findings.description: Full inventory: panes z-10/20/30, ContextMenu z-50 (ContextMenu.tsx:33), SwarmViewToggle z-[60], CommandPalette and AgentHUD z-[100], FileList/FileGrid dropdowns z-[999], SessionTypeSelector z-[9999] and SettingsModal zIndex 9999 (SettingsModal.tsx:287) tied, SwarmWizard and ToastContainer z-[99999]. Consequences: any context menu (z-50) opened while CommandPalette/AgentHUD (z-100) or a modal is up renders underneath; SettingsModal and SessionTypeSelector tie at 9999 so stacking depends on DOM order; each new overlay was clearly fixed by adding another 9.
findings.recommendation: Define a 5-level scale as CSS vars/Tailwind theme (content:0, sticky-chrome:10, popover:20, modal:30, toast:40), render all popovers/modals/toasts through portals into ordered root containers, and forbid arbitrary z-[N] values by lint. Portal ordering makes most z-index values unnecessary.

findings.title: Five different scrollbar treatments; the xterm viewport forces a permanently-visible 14px scrollbar that steals terminal columns
findings.description: Scrollbar zoo: global 7px accent-tinted (globals.css:63-82), .sidebar-scroll 2px (256-268), .ql-templates-scroll 6px white (dead code, 401-414), .scrollbar-hide, and .xterm-viewport with `overflow-y: scroll !important` + scrollbar-gutter: stable + 14px width (terminal.css:18-43). The forced `scroll` means every terminal pane always shows a 14px track — even a freshly-spawned empty shell — costing ~1.5 columns per pane in grid mode (at 5x2 that's 15 columns of lost width) and visually mismatching the 7px chrome scrollbars everywhere else.
findings.recommendation: Use overflow-y:auto with a slim overlay-style scrollbar (8px, transparent track, thumb only on hover/scroll), matching the app-wide 7px styling. WezTerm/Warp-tier terminals treat the scrollbar as an overlay affordance, not a reserved gutter.

findings.title: Sidebar spring animation reflows xterm every frame while refit timing assumes a fixed-duration animation that doesn't exist
findings.description: VibeSidebar animates width 0→320 with a spring (stiffness 400/damping 30 — no fixed duration, settles in ~500-700ms), forcing continuous layout of the adjacent terminal. AppLayout fires 'ghostshell:refit' once at a hardcoded 50ms (AppLayout.tsx:264-266, setTimeout with no cleanup) — mid-animation, useless. useTerminal's debouncedFit waits 300ms after the LAST resize event with a comment claiming it 'covers sidebar animation (250ms)' (useTerminal.ts:97) — a duration that matches neither the spring nor the .sidebar-transition CSS class (150ms, which is itself dead code). Net effect: terminal content is visibly mis-fit (wrong cols, reflowed TUI) for up to ~1s on every sidebar toggle, and the isElementVisible callback (useTerminal.ts:51-57) is dead code — defined, listed as a dependency of safeFit (line 87), never called.
findings.recommendation: Animate the sidebar with transform (translateX) over a fixed-size element, or animate a wrapper while the terminal region uses a CSS grid column that changes once at animation end (onAnimationComplete → single refit). Remove the redundant 50ms refit dispatch, clean up the timer, and delete isElementVisible. One authoritative resize path: ResizeObserver → single rAF-debounced fit.

findings.title: 'UI font size' setting rescales the entire app by mutating root font-size, distorting rem/px-mixed layout
findings.description: document.documentElement.style.fontSize = `${fontSize}px` (App.tsx:78-80, range 10-18) changes every rem unit — all Tailwind spacing/sizing (h-11 titlebar, p-4, gap-3, max-h-80) — while dozens of arbitrary px values (w-[320px] sidebar, w-[340px]/[360px] cards, height 320 monitor, min-w-[120px] tabs) stay fixed. At fontSize 10 or 18 the app becomes a mix of scaled and unscaled geometry: cramped titlebar vs oversized fixed cards, and every change forces xterm refits. This is layout scaling masquerading as a font setting.
findings.recommendation: Introduce a --ui-font-size var consumed only by typography (body { font-size: var(--ui-font-size) } with components using em/typographic tokens), or if whole-app zoom is the intent, use Electron's webFrame.setZoomFactor which scales px and rem coherently and is what real terminal apps (incl. VS Code) do.

findings.title: White-on-accent text becomes invisible on light-accent themes (Zero Lux, Monolith)
findings.description: MultiLineInput's Send button is `bg-[var(--ghost-accent)] ... text-white` (line 113) and UpdateBanner is `bg-ghost-accent text-white` (UpdateBanner.tsx:49). Themes zero-lux (accent #ffffff, themes.ts:588) and monolith (accent #e5ecf4, themes.ts:260) make these white-on-white — invisible label on the primary action. QuickLaunchRedesign got this right by using text-ghost-sidebar on accent fills (QuickLaunchRedesign.tsx:1084, 1124).
findings.recommendation: Add an --ghost-accent-contrast token computed in applyTheme (relative luminance threshold → near-black or near-white) and use it for all text-on-accent. Never pair text-white with a themable accent background.

findings.title: Inline style={{}} with color-mix() is the de-facto styling system in terminal chrome — unthemeable by Tailwind, recomputed every render
findings.description: TerminalCommandBar's render contains ~25 distinct inline style objects mixing color-mix(in srgb, var(--ghost-*) N%, rgba(...)) (lines 987-990, 1015-1019, 1033-1038, 1042-1053, 1071-1076, 1091-1101, 1106-1111, 1238-1241, 1254-1258, 1271-1279, 1288-1291, 1298-1301). TerminalPane header (365-368, 409-415, 486-491), TerminalTabs, MultiLineInput and TerminalSearch follow the same pattern, plus imperative style mutation in event handlers (MultiLineInput.tsx:101-108 sets borderColor/boxShadow on focus; TerminalPane.tsx:414-415 does the same; TerminalTabs.tsx:182-183 mutates color on mouseenter — hover state that React can clobber). Each render allocates fresh objects, defeats React memoization, bypasses the design system, and makes the hover/focus visuals unauditable.
findings.recommendation: Promote the ~8 recurring recipes (input surface, focused input, chip, selected row, hairline) to @layer components classes or CVA variants built on the token system, and express focus/hover via CSS :focus-within/:hover — no JS style mutation. This is also what makes a theme switch instant and consistent.

findings.title: Mixed Spanish/English UI copy and duplicated divergent tab-color palettes
findings.description: SessionTypeSelector card copy is Spanish ('Entorno individual potenciado por IA...', 'Orquestación multagente masiva...' lines 230, 257) while its own footer is English ('Abort sequence', 'Raw Terminal', lines 278-282); SwarmAgentCard shows 'Transmisión' (SwarmAgentCard.tsx:66); dead TerminalTabs is fully Spanish ('Renombrar', 'Cerrar', 'Vista de Cuadrícula') while the live GlobalDock is English. GlobalDock and TerminalTabs also define different TAB_COLORS palettes (9 muted customs vs 7 Tailwind-500s) and different fallback active colors (#4094e0 vs accent color-mix), so historical tab colors don't map between implementations.
findings.recommendation: Pick one language (or add an i18n layer) and one canonical TAB_COLORS constant exported from lib/. This is the kind of drift that screams multiple AI sessions with no shared glossary — a rebuild should centralize user-facing strings from day one.

findings.title: Dead/unused visual logic inside live components: unused footerText with mojibake scrub, exit animations that can never play
findings.description: footerText (line 978) applies replaceAll('Ã‚Â·', '·') — a UTF-8-decoded-as-Latin-1 mojibake bandaid — and is then never used (displayFooterText at 980-982 is rendered instead). SessionTypeSelector wraps its own always-rendered content in AnimatePresence (lines 191-286): exit variants on every motion element are dead because the component unmounts synchronously when the parent removes it — AnimatePresence must wrap the conditional in the PARENT (GlobalDock/TerminalContainer render it bare at GlobalDock.tsx:353-358). ToastContainer similarly returns null when empty (ToastContainer.tsx:118) before AnimatePresence can run the last toast's exit animation.
findings.recommendation: Delete footerText and fix the encoding at the source (the file is otherwise clean UTF-8). Move AnimatePresence to the owners of the conditionals so exit animations actually run, or remove the exit props to stop pretending.

findings.title: Terminal canvas polish gaps: 4px/6px padding, invisible 1px pane gaps, weak active-pane indication, rounded drop overlay on square panes
findings.description: .xterm padding is 4px 6px (terminal.css:3) — FitAddon does subtract it, but it's visibly cramped against the pane header and asymmetric vs the 12px chrome padding elsewhere. BentoLayout separates panes with a 1px gap whose color is the same bg-ghost-bg as the panes (BentoLayout.tsx:69-75), so grid-mode separators are invisible and adjacent terminals visually merge; the only active-pane cue is header title opacity (text-white/80 vs /45, TerminalPane.tsx:424) — no border/accent on the focused pane like WezTerm/Warp. The drag-drop overlay has border-radius 14px (terminal.css:96) inside square-cornered panes, so the dashed border floats 14px off the actual pane corners.
findings.recommendation: Bump terminal padding to a token (8-10px), give the grid gap a hairline color (var(--ghost-border)) with an accent left-edge or border on the focused pane, and match the drop overlay radius to the real pane radius (0).

findings.title: Stale pre-redesign palette leftovers: slate/indigo hovers and hardcoded slate dot colors
findings.description: Toggle.tsx:15 and ContextMenu.tsx:49 use hover:bg-slate-800/50; RangeSlider.tsx:15 uses bg-indigo-950/50 for its value pill (indigo = the old Qubria accent); QuickLaunchRedesign LayoutDots hardcodes '#475569' slate for inactive dots (QuickLaunchRedesign.tsx:84). All are invisible-to-wrong on non-navy themes and are the only slate/indigo references left in common components.
findings.recommendation: Replace with token equivalents (hover:bg-white/[0.05], bg-ghost-accent/10, var(--ghost-text-dim)). Add these to the same hex/palette lint ban as the #38bdf8 sweep.

findings.title: Custom keyboard shortcuts never persist: StateStorage passed where PersistStorage is required
findings.description: `storage: electronStorage as any` hands zustand v5's persist a string-based StateStorage where it requires an object-based PersistStorage (every other store correctly wraps it: settingsStore.ts:368, workspaceStore.ts:151, historyStore.ts:245). On save, persist calls setItem(name, {state, version}) with an OBJECT; electronStorage.setItem (electronStorage.ts:26-38) does JSON.parse(value) on that object, which throws SyntaxError on '[object Object]', is swallowed by the catch, and nothing is written. On load, getItem returns a JSON string (or null), persist reads `.state`/`.version` off it and gets undefined, so defaults hydrate. Net effect: every rebind, disabled binding, and conflict repair the user makes in ShortcutsTab is silently lost on restart. The `as any` cast is the tell — the type system flagged exactly this and was overridden.
findings.recommendation: Replace with `storage: createJSONStorage(() => electronStorage)` like the other stores, add a regression test that round-trips an override through the storage adapter, and ban `as any` on persist options.

findings.title: Maximize and tabs/grid view-switch unmount panes and kill their live PTYs
findings.description: PTY lifetime is coupled to React mount: usePty's cleanup unconditionally calls ptyKill (usePty.ts:1570) and pty-manager.create() kills any existing PTY with the same id (electron/pty-manager.ts:153-155). But two state-driven render paths hide panes by UNMOUNTING them: (1) when maximizedSessionId is set, BentoLayout.tsx:59-65 renders only the maximized pane, so Ctrl+Shift+Enter in a multi-pane workspace destroys every other agent's shell process — and because the maximize branch also changes the wrapper structure, even the maximized pane's own TerminalPane remounts and its PTY is killed and respawned; (2) TerminalContainer.tsx:111-123 keys workspaces by first-session-id in tabs mode but by the literal 'grid-view' in grid mode, so clicking the Tabs/Grid toggle (TerminalTabs.tsx:100/107) remounts every pane and restarts every shell/agent, losing all context. The stable-key comment at TerminalContainer.tsx:115-121 proves the author knew remount = PTY death, and only patched the split-promotion case. Tabs mode itself does it right (hidden class, AppLayout.tsx:291-296 keeps terminals mounted behind the dashboard).
findings.recommendation: Adopt the WezTerm mux model: a session/PTY registry that owns process lifetime keyed by session id, killed only by explicit removeSession — never by component unmount. All layout modes (tabs, grid, maximize) must render every live pane and hide with CSS (visibility/display), exactly as tabs mode and the dashboard overlay already do.

findings.title: Three uncoordinated keyboard layers: rebindable registry, hardcoded xterm intercepts, and a rogue Ctrl+Space listener
findings.description: Layer 1: useKeyboardShortcuts is a window bubble-phase keydown handler that bails on event.defaultPrevented (line 60) and deliberately treats .xterm as non-editable (line 29). Layer 2: usePty.ts:1026-1125 attachCustomKeyEventHandler hardcodes Ctrl+T (line 1112), F2 (1120), Shift+Enter, Ctrl+C/V — ignoring the shortcut registry entirely, so rebinding 'New Terminal' away from Ctrl+T does nothing while a terminal is focused. Layer 3: TerminalContainer.tsx:28-37 registers its own raw Ctrl+Space listener that is not in the registry, ignores defaultPrevented and editable targets, so it opens the AgentHUD while typing in the rename input or the settings modal, while xterm simultaneously sends NUL (\x00) to the shell. The systemic result: whether a registry shortcut works while the terminal has focus depends on xterm's internal evaluateKeyboardEvent per combo — Ctrl+L, Ctrl+PageUp/PageDown, Ctrl+Home/End, Ctrl+Shift+PageUp/PageDown are consumed by xterm (escape bytes go to the PTY, preventDefault kills layer 1), and Ctrl+2..Ctrl+8 (tab.2–tab.8) send NUL/ESC/FS control bytes into the CLI instead of switching tabs, while Ctrl+1 and Ctrl+9 happen to work. That can cancel a running Claude prompt with ESC when the user just wanted tab 3.
findings.recommendation: One dispatch table: resolve bindings from shortcutStore in a single capture-phase handler, and drive xterm's attachCustomKeyEventHandler from that same table (return false for any combo the app owns). Delete the TerminalContainer listener and register Ctrl+Space in the registry. This is how WezTerm treats key assignments: one keymap, terminal passthrough only for unbound keys.

findings.title: Async persist hydration is never awaited: restoreTabs race and theme/font flash on every launch
findings.description: settingsStore persists through async IPC (electronStorage → ipcRenderer.invoke), so hydration completes some time after first render, yet nothing in the app gates on it (zero uses of hasHydrated/onFinishHydration anywhere). AppLayout's restore effect reads useSettingsStore.getState().restoreTabs at mount (line 133) — before hydration, that is the default `true`, so a user who disabled tab restore can still get tabs restored (e.g. after a crash left a stale snapshot, since clearTabSnapshot only runs on graceful close). Likewise App.tsx:17-19 applies the default 'qubria-dark' theme and default font size immediately, then onRehydrateStorage (settingsStore.ts:399-406) re-applies the real theme — a visible theme/typography flash on every cold start when the user's theme differs from the default.
findings.recommendation: Gate startup on hydration: await useSettingsStore.persist.onFinishHydration (or render a splash until all persisted stores report hasHydrated), then run tab restore and theme application once, with real values.

findings.title: commandBlockStore never releases data for closed sessions (unbounded growth across the app's lifetime)
findings.description: blocksBySession/activeBlockBySession are keyed by session id and capped per session (300 blocks × 24k chars output + 36k chars rawOutput ≈ up to ~18 MB of strings per session), but nothing removes a session's entry when the session closes: usePty's unmount cleanup removes the activity record (usePty.ts:1560) and the companion session (usePty.ts:1568) yet never touches command blocks; clearSession is only invoked from a manual UI button (CommandBlocksPanel.tsx:174). A day of opening/closing agent tabs accumulates every dead session's block history in memory until app restart. Contrast with companionStore.removeSession and activityStore.removeAgent, which do the right thing.
findings.recommendation: Delete the session's block state in the same cleanup path that removes companion/activity state (or better: centralize all per-session teardown in terminalStore.removeSession so no store can be forgotten).

findings.title: All 'open settings tab' shortcuts land on the Appearance tab due to `??` after a void optional call
findings.description: Each settings shortcut runs `onOpenSettingsTab?.(tab) ?? onNavigate?.('settings')` (lines 438-467). onOpenSettingsTab returns void, i.e. undefined, so the nullish-coalescing right side ALWAYS executes too: handleNavigate('settings') → openSettings() with the default 'appearance' tab (AppLayout.tsx:57-60, 79-82), overwriting the tab that was just set in the same batch. Ctrl+Shift+, (Terminal tab), Ctrl+Alt+, (Providers) and Ctrl+Alt+K (Shortcuts) all open on Appearance. The intent was clearly 'call A if present, else B'.
findings.recommendation: Use explicit branching: `if (onOpenSettingsTab) onOpenSettingsTab(tab); else onNavigate?.('settings')`. Add an ESLint rule flagging `??` on void-returning calls.

findings.title: Triple session/group/workspace abstraction with stored-but-dead derived state and O(n·m) recomputation everywhere
findings.description: The model is sessions + groups + a derived 'workspace' list rebuilt by buildWorkspaces (which itself re-runs normalizeGroups) at 15+ call sites: inside nearly every store action (lines 160, 170, 241, 266, 298, 312, 375, 538, 601, 622), in two components' useMemos (TerminalContainer.tsx:71, GlobalDock.tsx:93), and on every matching keydown (useKeyboardShortcuts.ts:315, 341, 373, 400, 418). `activeGroupId` is documented as 'legacy compatibility' (line 18-19) and is written in ~20 return objects, but a repo-wide search shows it is never read outside the store and its tests — pure dead state that every action must remember to maintain. setActiveGroup, removeGroup and removeSessionFromGroup are never called from any component. removeSession (158-210) and closeWorkspace (296-357) duplicate ~50 lines of near-identical focus-fallback logic. The name 'workspace' also collides with workspaceStore's unrelated project-folder Workspace. Test coverage exists only for closeWorkspace (terminalStore.test.ts) — none for removeSession fallback, normalizeGroups, addGroup, or duplicateSession.
findings.recommendation: Rebuild around one primary entity — a Tab (workspace) with an ordered list of pane/session ids, allowed to hold a single pane (WezTerm's tab→pane model). Derive the tab list with a memoized selector in one place, delete activeGroupId and the dead group actions, and extract the shared 'pick next focus after close' helper used by both close paths.

findings.title: normalizeGroups auto-dissolving <2-session groups changes workspace identity mid-flight
findings.description: Any group falling below 2 sessions is silently deleted (line 67 `if (cleaned.length < 2) continue`), so the surviving session's workspace id flips from group.id to session.id. Downstream code has to fight this identity churn: TerminalContainer.tsx:115-122 keys the React subtree by first-session-id specifically 'so that... TerminalPane [does not remount] — which would dispose xterm and kill the PTY', and removeSession must diff previous vs next workspace lists (terminalStore.ts:160-184) to keep focus sane. addGroup also refuses groups with <2 members (line 507), which is why AppLayout's snapshot restore silently drops a group whose second session failed to map (AppLayout.tsx:200). The invariant creates the exact instability the rest of the code patches around.
findings.recommendation: Give tabs stable ids independent of member count — a tab containing one pane is a perfectly valid state (this is how WezTerm, iTerm2 and VS Code model it). This deletes the stable-key hack, the previous/next diffing, and the restore edge case in one move.

findings.title: Non-atomic JSON storage writes + 3s force-close can corrupt or silently wipe persisted state
findings.description: storage:set writes with a direct fs.writeFile (main.ts:613) — no temp-file+rename, no backup. The close handshake force-destroys the window after 3s (main.ts:208-211), and a crash/power loss can also interrupt a write, leaving a truncated JSON file. storage:get (main.ts:594-604) catches the resulting parse error and returns null, so the renderer silently hydrates factory defaults — settings, history, workspaces or the tab snapshot vanish with no error surfaced to the user. electronStorage.getItem additionally maps any falsy stored value to null (electronStorage.ts:12).
findings.recommendation: Write atomically (write `${file}.tmp`, fsync, rename), keep the previous file as .bak and fall back to it on parse failure, and surface a corruption notification instead of silently resetting.

findings.title: Session restore is one-shot and crash-fragile; restored agent tabs come back as dead shells
findings.description: The tab snapshot is written only inside onBeforeClose (App.tsx:26-42) and deleted immediately when consumed at startup (AppLayout.tsx:139 `await clearTabSnapshot()` before restoring). Any crash, task-kill, GPU wedge, or Windows shutdown that skips the handshake loses the entire layout — and because the snapshot was already cleared at the previous startup, there is no stale copy to fall back to. What does restore is shallow: sessions are recreated with skipAutoLaunch:true (AppLayout.tsx:186) and agents forced 'offline' (AppLayout.tsx:167), so agent tabs reopen as plain empty shells with no scrollback and no relaunched CLI; the hasConversation/--continue plumbing only helps if the user manually restarts each agent.
findings.recommendation: Checkpoint the snapshot on a debounced interval and on every session/group mutation (WezTerm/tmux-style resurrection), keep the last snapshot until a newer one is written, and on restore offer one-click 'relaunch agents' that replays buildLaunchCommand with --continue.

findings.title: Date.now()-based IDs with no duplicate guard in addSession
findings.description: IDs are minted from wall-clock time in many hot paths: `term-split-${Date.now()}` (terminalStore.ts:452), `group-${Date.now()}` (terminalStore.ts:484, useAgent.ts:312), `ws-${Date.now()}` (workspaceStore.ts:97), `term-standalone/quicklaunch-${Date.now()}` (AppLayout.tsx:100/111, TerminalContainer.tsx:43/99, GlobalDock.tsx:165, CommandPalette.tsx:88, FileExplorer.tsx:271). Two calls in the same millisecond (double-fired event, programmatic loops, or a future batch path) produce identical ids. addSession (terminalStore.ts:143-156) does not reject duplicates, and the consequences are nasty: duplicate React keys, and pty-manager.create() killing the first session's live PTY when the second registers the same id (pty-manager.ts:153-155). Some sites already hedge with a random suffix (AppLayout.tsx:175, QuickLaunchRedesign.tsx:584) — the inconsistency shows the risk was noticed but never fixed at the source.
findings.recommendation: Mint ids with crypto.randomUUID() in a single idFactory module, and make addSession throw/no-op on duplicate ids as a store invariant.

findings.title: 'Reopen Closed Tab' only records keyboard-initiated closes
findings.description: closedTabStack is a module-level array populated exclusively inside the terminal.close shortcut handler (lines 101-121). Closing a tab via the pane's X button (TerminalContainer.tsx:143 → removeSession), the tab strip, closeWorkspace, or agent stop paths never pushes an entry, so Ctrl+Shift+T usually reopens nothing — or worse, reopens a tab from several closes ago, which reads as random behavior. Agent tabs are excluded entirely (line 108-111 routes to stopAgent and returns before pushing).
findings.recommendation: Move the closed-tab ring buffer into terminalStore and record it inside removeSession/closeWorkspace so every close path feeds it, including enough agent config to relaunch.

findings.title: activityStore.tasks grows without a cap, unlike every sibling list
findings.description: The store carefully caps filesTouched (200), activityLog (100), subAgents (50) and outputLines (200), but addTask appends with `[...existing.tasks, newTask]` (line 258) with no slice. A long-running Claude session that emits many task_create events (multi-hour agent runs are this app's core use case) accumulates tasks indefinitely, and every subsequent updateTask maps over the whole array.
findings.recommendation: Add MAX_TASKS with the same `.slice(-N)` pattern, or compact completed tasks beyond a threshold.

findings.title: Shortcut capture accepts bare printable keys that then fire while typing in the terminal
findings.description: The recorder only rejects modifier-only presses and 4 reserved combos (ShortcutsTab.tsx:232-246, shortcutRegistry.ts:157-167); a bare letter like 'a' is a valid binding. Meanwhile isEditableTarget deliberately returns false for .xterm (useKeyboardShortcuts.ts:29) so global shortcuts stay armed while the terminal is focused, and xterm does not preventDefault plain printable keydowns — so a bare-letter binding both types the character into the shell AND triggers the action on every keystroke. The same .xterm exemption is also why F2 rename works in-terminal, so it can't simply be removed.
findings.recommendation: Require at least one modifier for non-function keys at capture time, and validate again in the store (assignBinding) so persisted data can't smuggle bare keys in.

findings.title: The window CustomEvent bus is a hidden global architecture with scattered, duplicated identifiers
findings.description: Command routing happens over 15 window events: the 12 SHORTCUT_EVENTS (dispatched from useKeyboardShortcuts, CommandPalette.tsx:219-425, and usePty.ts:1114; listened per-pane in TerminalPane.tsx:178-267 gated by an isActive prop convention, plus TerminalContainer.tsx:55-56) and 3 ad-hoc strings outside the registry: 'ghostshell:refit' (AppLayout.tsx:265 → useTerminal.ts:210), 'ghostshell:open-settings' (TerminalTabs.tsx:179 → AppLayout.tsx:270), and 'ghostshell:focus-command-bar', whose literal is copy-pasted into three files (usePty.ts:34, TerminalPane.tsx:22, TerminalCommandBar.tsx:68). Correctness depends on invisible conventions: exactly one pane having isActive at dispatch time (zero handlers if focus state is transitioning, N handlers if two panes briefly both believe they're active), no payload typing, and no discoverability of who handles what.
findings.recommendation: Replace the bus with explicit store-level commands (e.g. terminalStore.commands.clearActive()) or, minimally, a single typed emitter module owning every event name and payload type — no string literals at call sites.

findings.title: Dead code in App.tsx: unused LaunchScreen, AnimatePresence, and launchMode state
findings.description: App.tsx imports AnimatePresence (line 2) and LaunchScreen (line 4) and declares `const [launchMode, setLaunchMode] = useState<LaunchMode | null>(null)` (line 15), none of which are used — the render is just ErrorBoundary + AppLayout. LaunchScreen.tsx is an orphaned component with no other importer. Remnants of an abandoned launch-mode flow left in the entry file.
findings.recommendation: Delete the state, the imports, and LaunchScreen.tsx (or wire the flow back in intentionally). Enable noUnusedLocals / eslint-plugin-unused-imports in CI.

findings.title: openMultiLineInput event is never dispatched — the entire MultiLineInput overlay is unreachable
findings.description: SHORTCUT_EVENTS.openMultiLineInput (shortcutEvents.ts:6) has a listener in TerminalPane (lines 203-209) that opens the MultiLineInput overlay, and ~40 lines of provider-aware submission logic (handleMultiLineSubmit, lines 270-306, including the Claude '\'+Enter continuation dance), but a repo-wide search finds zero dispatchers. Shift+Enter multiline is handled natively in usePty instead (usePty.ts:1074-1077). Dead feature carried by every pane render.
findings.recommendation: Delete the event, listener, overlay wiring, and MultiLineInput usage — or resurrect it as a command-palette action if the fallback is still wanted for non-TUI shells.

findings.title: TerminalSession.isActive is a required field that is never read
findings.description: isActive is required on TerminalSession, set to a constant `true` in addSession (terminalStore.ts:144) and duplicateSession (terminalStore.ts:458), never updated when the active session changes (that is activeSessionId's job), and never read anywhere in the codebase — tests must fabricate it (terminalStore.test.ts:10). It also forces the awkward `Omit<TerminalSession, 'isActive'>` signature on addSession.
findings.recommendation: Remove the field from the type, the store, and the tests. Active-ness is already derived from activeSessionId.

findings.title: agentStore persists agents to localStorage only to wipe them (via direct state mutation) on every hydration
findings.description: agentStore uses persist with no storage option — so it writes to localStorage, inconsistent with every other store's electronStorage — and then onRehydrateStorage sets state.agents = [] by direct in-place mutation (lines 83-88) because 'PTY processes don't survive app restart'. Every agent mutation pays serialization cost for data that is discarded by design, the mutation bypasses subscriber notification, and the module-level `nextId` counter (line 20) resets on restart, leaving Date.now()+counter as the only uniqueness guarantee.
findings.recommendation: Drop persist from agentStore entirely (tabSnapshot already captures what should survive), or partialize to nothing. If any agent metadata should persist, do it through the snapshot path deliberately.

findings.title: Command-block boundaries and success/failure are guessed from prompt regexes and the word 'error'
findings.description: finalizeBlock strips the echoed command by building a RegExp from the command text and deletes any trailing line ending in '>', '$' or '#' (lines 76-86) — which also eats legitimate output (a final line like '#endif' or 'C:\>' printed by the program itself). Status is decided by errorHints: any chunk matching /\berror\b/i, 'failed', 'exception', etc. (lines 37-46, 93) marks the whole block 'error' — so `npm test` output that PASSES while printing 'expected error' is reported failed, and real failures with exit code 1 but quiet output are reported success. There is no exit-code signal at all because block start/finish are inferred from prompt-shaped lines (usePty side) instead of shell integration.
findings.recommendation: Implement OSC 133 (A/B/C/D) shell integration for PowerShell and bash like WezTerm/Warp/Windows Terminal: exact command boundaries, real exit codes, and the entire heuristic layer (echo stripping, prompt regexes, error-word sniffing) gets deleted.

findings.title: workspaceStore Windows path handling: deprecated navigator.platform, 'C:\\Users' fallback, case-sensitive dedupe
findings.description: DEFAULT_PATH sniffs the deprecated navigator.platform and hardcodes 'C:\\Users' as the universal Windows fallback (line 20) — new terminals then spawn in a directory the user almost never wants; the real home dir is available via shellGetHomedir but unused here. pickPath silently substitutes this fallback for empty input in setCurrentPath (line 128). recentProjects dedupe compares raw strings (sanitizeRecentProjects lines 52-56, setCurrentPath line 129), but Windows paths are case-insensitive, so 'c:\\dev\\app' and 'C:\\Dev\\App' occupy two of the ten recent slots. historyStore already has a normalizePath that lowercases (historyStore.ts:32-34) — the logic exists but isn't shared.
findings.recommendation: Resolve the default cwd from shellGetHomedir at startup, and dedupe recents on a normalized (lowercased, separator-normalized) key while preserving display casing — reuse historyStore's normalizePath from a shared path util.

findings.title: Notification dedupe merge reorders toasts and the cap can silently drop persistent notifications
findings.description: When a duplicate arrives inside the dedupe window, the existing notification is filtered out and re-appended at the end of the array (line 158), so the toast visually jumps to a new position in the stack each time its count increments — flicker/jank in the toast column. Separately, trimVisibleNotifications (lines 103-111) drops the first entry when no non-persistent one exists, meaning a 6th persistent notification silently evicts an older persistent one that was, by contract, supposed to stay until dismissed.
findings.recommendation: Update the merged notification in place (map, not filter+append) to keep stack order stable, and overflow persistent notifications into a collapsible 'N more' group instead of deleting them.

findings.title: Every keystroke walks a ~45-branch if-chain with linear registry scans
findings.description: handleKeyDown runs on every window keydown — including each character typed into the terminal, since .xterm targets are exempted from the editable check (line 29). For every event it sequentially calls matches() for up to ~45 shortcut ids; each matches() calls getActiveBindings → getShortcutDef, which is a linear find over the ~60-entry SHORTCUT_REGISTRY (shortcutRegistry.ts:565-567), plus per-binding normalization. That is thousands of comparisons and dozens of transient array/object allocations per keystroke to conclude 'not a shortcut'. Not user-visible today, but it is the opposite of a dispatch table and every new shortcut adds another sequential branch.
findings.recommendation: Precompute a Map<comboSignature, shortcutId> whenever overrides change (the signature function already exists: getKeyComboSignature), and resolve each keydown with one lookup. This also collapses the 400-line if-chain into a declarative action table.

strengths: settingsStore persistence hygiene is genuinely good: normalizePersistedSettings (settingsStore.ts:256-294) type-guards and clamps every field, sanitizes savedAgents/launchPresets with dedupe, and is applied in both migrate and merge — corrupted or hand-edited storage can't poison the store. Keep this pattern as the template for all stores.

useTerminal.ts live-sync is near WezTerm quality: a single settings subscription with prevState diffing (lines 302-347), termRef nulled before dispose so concurrent subscribers bail safely (line 222), WebGL context-loss fallback to the DOM renderer (lines 113-133), and scroll-position-preserving fit that respects 'user is reading scrollback' (lines 60-87). Preserve all of it.

The graceful-close handshake (window 'close' → app:before-close → renderer saves snapshot → app:close-ready → destroy, with a 3s force timeout; electron/main.ts:199-212, App.tsx:22-42) is the right shape for save-on-exit — it just needs crash-resilient checkpointing on top.

The shortcut registry as data (shortcutRegistry.ts SHORTCUT_REGISTRY with categories, readonly xterm-owned bindings, alternate bindings, reserved combos, and conflict detection/repair in shortcutStore) is the correct architecture for rebindable keys — the failures are in wiring (persistence cast, bypassing layers), not in the model.

Memory-cap discipline exists in most ring buffers: MAX_BLOCKS_PER_SESSION/MAX_OUTPUT_CHARS (commandBlockStore.ts:35-36), MAX_SESSION_ENTRIES with time-windowed dedupe (companionStore.ts:44-45), MAX_FILE_TOUCHES/MAX_ACTIVITY_LOG/MAX_SUB_AGENTS/MAX_OUTPUT_LINES (activityStore.ts:32-36), history capped at 500 (historyStore.ts:203) — the leak findings are gaps in an otherwise conscious policy.

Per-session teardown in usePty's cleanup (usePty.ts:1552-1574) correctly unwinds activity state, companion entries, timers, the batch parser, and the window output buffer — the discipline is there, just not centralized.

AppLayout keeps terminals mounted behind the swarm dashboard using the 'invisible' class with an explicit comment about preserving PTYs (AppLayout.tsx:291-296), and tabs mode hides inactive workspaces with CSS instead of unmounting (TerminalContainer.tsx:111-113) — this is exactly the technique the maximize/grid paths should have used.

notificationStore's pause/resume with remainingMs bookkeeping, dedupe-key merging with count, and centralized removal timers (notificationStore.ts:57-111, 220-260) is a more thoughtful toast system than most apps ship.

The store-level focus-fallback tests for closeWorkspace (terminalStore.test.ts) target real regression-prone behavior (adjacent-tab focus, group dissolution) — the right kind of test, there just aren't enough of them.
analyses.summary: State lives in nine Zustand stores: terminalStore holds a sessions+groups model from which a third 'workspace' (tab) abstraction is re-derived at 15+ call sites, with a dead activeGroupId mirror maintained everywhere; persistence goes through an async Electron-IPC storage adapter that most stores wrap correctly but shortcutStore passes raw with an `as any` cast, silently breaking all keybinding persistence. Commands flow over a hidden window-CustomEvent bus (12 registry events plus 3 ad-hoc strings), and keyboard input is handled by three uncoordinated layers (global keydown chain, hardcoded xterm intercepts in usePty, a rogue Ctrl+Space listener) whose interaction decides — per xterm internals — which shortcuts work and which leak control bytes into the PTY. Session continuity is a one-shot tabSnapshot written only on graceful close, restored before async settings hydration finishes, and the PTY lifecycle is coupled to React mount so maximize and tabs↔grid switching literally kill running agent shells. The individual stores show real craft (sanitization, caps, live-sync diffing); the systemic failures are in the seams between them."

Build tooling is electron-vite 2 (Vite 5) with three tsconfigs (base strict:true, web, node), vitest 4 for tests, and a tag-triggered GitHub Actions release workflow that packages with electron-builder. Nothing in the pipeline actually gates quality: the build is esbuild transpile-only (no tsc), CI never runs `npm test` or `tsc --noEmit`, and there is no lint tooling at all. As a result HEAD ships with a real TS compile error that becomes a runtime ReferenceError in the packaged app, a permanently red test suite, ~11,300 lines of never-imported components, duplicate build configs, and four dead npm dependencies. Test coverage is inverted relative to risk: the swarm library layer has an excellent 2,082-line integration suite, while every terminal-critical module (usePty, useTerminal, pty-manager, claude-output-parser, terminalOutputEnhancer, 12 of 13 stores) has zero tests.
strengths: TypeScript strict:true is enabled for BOTH renderer and main process (C:/Users/chitu/Desktop/GhostShell-main/tsconfig.json:7) and the 69k-line codebase compiles with only a single error under it — the baseline type hygiene is genuinely good and worth preserving.

The swarm library layer has a substantial, well-organized integration test suite: src/lib/__tests__/swarm-integration.test.ts (2,082 lines, 18 describe blocks covering codebase-analyzer, mission-planner, conflict-detector, self-heal, checkpoints, autonomy, operator, etc.), 85 passing tests running in ~8.5s on vitest 4.

scripts/ensure-electron-install.js is a thoughtful Windows-specific guard: it verifies the Electron binary matches package version/platform and self-repairs corrupted installs (common with OneDrive/AV interference), and fixes node-pty spawn-helper permissions cross-platform.

Native module packaging is done correctly: node-pty 1.1.0 with N-API prebuilds (win32-x64/arm64 present in node_modules/node-pty/prebuilds), asarUnpack for node-pty and npmRebuild:false in electron-builder.yml:13-16 — no Visual Studio toolchain needed to package, which is exactly right for Windows distribution.

electron/preload.ts uses proper contextBridge isolation, typed IPC wrappers, listener registrations that return cleanup functions (preload.ts:19-28), and exports `GhostShellAPI = typeof api` (preload.ts:122) — the right pattern, even though the renderer doesn't consume it.
electron-vite main/preload/renderer separation with externalizeDepsPlugin and per-target rollup inputs is the correct Electron architecture; production build completes cleanly in ~6s.

findings.title: Shipped TypeScript error is a runtime ReferenceError that breaks Enter in plain-shell sessions
findings.description: `npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.web.json` fails with TS2304: Cannot find name 'inputBuffer' at usePty.ts:523. `trackCommandSubmission` (defined at line 502 in the useEffect scope) assigns `inputBuffer = ''`, but the variable is declared at line 950 (`let inputBuffer = ''`) INSIDE the nested `init` async function (line 736) — a sibling scope. I verified the production bundle (out/renderer/assets/index-*.js): Rollup renamed the inner declaration to `inputBuffer2` and left the outer assignment as a bare `inputBuffer = ""` to an undeclared identifier. The bundle loads via <script type="module"> (strict mode), so every time Enter is pressed in a non-provider shell session, onData (line 1428) calls trackCommandSubmission which throws ReferenceError AFTER registering the prompt submission but BEFORE the `\r` is forwarded to the PTY (lines 1441-1451 never run) — the keystroke is swallowed and command-block tracking corrupts.
findings.recommendation: Hoist `let inputBuffer = ''` from init() scope (line 950) to the useEffect scope next to promptTail so trackCommandSubmission can reset it. Then add `"typecheck": "tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.web.json && tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.node.json"` to package.json and make the build script run it — esbuild/Vite will happily ship scope bugs like this forever otherwise.

findings.title: No typecheck, test, or lint gate anywhere in the build or release pipeline
findings.description: The only CI workflow (release.yml) triggers on tags and runs `npm ci` → `npx electron-vite build` → `npx electron-builder` → publishes — it never runs `npm test` or `tsc --noEmit`. package.json has no `typecheck` or `lint` script at all, and there is no ESLint/Prettier config in the repo (electron-builder.yml:10 even excludes `.eslintrc.cjs`/`.prettierrc.yaml` files that don't exist — copied template). electron-vite uses esbuild which strips types without checking, so the TS2304 error above and the failing test both shipped in v2.2.0. Bonus: release.yml:27 sets `npm_config_node_linker: hoisted`, a pnpm-only option that is a no-op under npm ci.
findings.recommendation: Add a CI workflow on push/PR that runs typecheck + vitest + eslint (typescript-eslint with react-hooks plugin), and make the release job depend on it. WezTerm-quality means a red main is impossible, not merely discouraged.

findings.title: Test suite is permanently red: stale test asserts behavior the implementation deliberately removed
findings.description: `npm test` fails at HEAD: 1 failed / 85 passed. terminalTextInput.test.ts:10-12 expects `shouldCaptureStructuredTextInsertion('insertFromPaste'|'insertReplacementText'|'insertFromDrop', 'hello')` to return true, but src/lib/terminalTextInput.ts:14-24 was rewritten to only capture `insertText` with length > 1 — the comment at lines 18-21 explicitly says intercepting insertFromPaste caused double paste writes and was removed. The test was never updated. A suite that is red on a clean checkout trains everyone to ignore failures, which is how the critical usePty bug survived.
findings.recommendation: Rewrite the test to assert the CURRENT contract: insertFromPaste/insertReplacementText/insertFromDrop return false, insertText >1 char returns true. Then enforce green tests in CI so behavior changes must update their tests in the same commit.

findings.title: Zero test coverage for every terminal-critical module; vitest config makes main-process and DOM testing impossible
findings.description: Coverage inventory: usePty.ts (1,576 lines — PTY lifecycle, provider detection heuristics, command-block state machine, ~30 regexes): 0 tests. useTerminal.ts (394): 0. electron/pty-manager.ts (298 — ConPTY/winpty fallback ladder): 0, and it CANNOT be tested because vitest include is 'src/**/__tests__/**/*.test.ts' (line 8), which excludes electron/**. claude-output-parser.ts (886): 0. terminalOutputEnhancer.ts (147): 0. 12 of 13 zustand stores: 0 (terminalStore.test.ts covers only closeWorkspace, 3 cases of a 655-line store). environment is 'node' (line 7) with no jsdom/happy-dom dependency and no @testing-library, so hooks/components are untestable as configured. The heuristic-heaviest, regression-prone code (prompt detection, idle detection, completion debouncing) has no safety net at all.
findings.recommendation: Extract the pure logic out of usePty.ts (prompt/idle/working regex matching, isLikelyPrompt, detectProviderFromCommand, completion timing state machine) into testable modules and snapshot-test them against captured real CLI output (Claude Code, Gemini, Codex, PowerShell, bash transcripts). Add a second vitest project with environment jsdom for hooks, and widen include to electron/**/__tests__ for pty-manager with node-pty mocked.

findings.title: `electronStorage as any` passes the wrong storage interface to zustand persist — shortcut overrides silently never persist
findings.description: Every other persisted store wraps electronStorage in `createJSONStorage(() => electronStorage)` (historyStore.ts:245, modelStore.ts:334, settingsStore.ts:368, swarmStore.ts:1121), but shortcutStore.ts:339 does `storage: electronStorage as any`. zustand v5's `storage` option requires PersistStorage (object-based `{state, version}`), while electronStorage (src/lib/electronStorage.ts:8) is a string-based StateStorage. At runtime persist calls setItem with an OBJECT; electronStorage.setItem:28 runs `JSON.parse(value)` on it → JSON.parse("[object Object]") throws SyntaxError → swallowed by the catch at line 35 with only a console.error → writes never happen. getItem returns a JSON string where persist expects an object, so `.state` is undefined and hydration is a no-op. Custom keyboard shortcuts are lost on every restart, and the `as any` cast is precisely what hid it from the compiler.
findings.recommendation: Change to `storage: createJSONStorage(() => electronStorage)` like the other stores, delete the cast, and add a lint rule banning `as any` in src/stores. Add a persistence round-trip test for each persisted store.

findings.title: Electron 33.4.11 is past end-of-life with 18 unpatched advisories; js-yaml moderate DoS in prod deps
findings.description: `npm audit --omit=dev` reports electron <=39.8.4 HIGH severity with 18 advisories including ASAR integrity bypass (GHSA-vmqv-hx8q-j7mg), registry key path injection in setAsDefaultProtocolClient on Windows (GHSA-mwmh-mq4g-g6gr), several use-after-frees, and HTTP response header injection; plus js-yaml 4.x moderate quadratic DoS (GHSA-h67p-54hq-rp68, used by electron-updater to parse latest.yml). Electron 33 (Chromium 130, Oct 2024) stopped receiving security backports over a year ago as of July 2026. For an app whose index.html also loads remote resources (Google Fonts) and whose whole purpose is executing AI agents with shell access, running an EOL Chromium is a real exposure, not audit noise.
findings.recommendation: Upgrade to a supported Electron line (npm audit suggests 43.x) — with contextIsolation already in place the migration cost is mostly API deprecations. Establish a policy of tracking the newest-stable-minus-one Electron, and add `npm audit --omit=dev --audit-level=high` to CI.

findings.title: ~11,300 lines (34 files, ~16% of src) of never-imported dead components, plus a dead LaunchScreen feature
findings.description: 34 source files are imported by nothing: SwarmDebrief.tsx (1,056 lines), SwarmCommandCenter.tsx (937), AgentCreator.tsx (555), TerminalTabs.tsx (366 — an entire abandoned tab bar implementation), FloatingSidePanel.tsx, all six Swarm wizard steps (SwarmNameStep/MissionStep/DirectoryStep/ContextStep/PlanStep/RosterStep), SwarmTaskBoard, SwarmApprovalQueue, SwarmInterviewPanel, CodebaseGraph, StatusBadge, ResizeHandle, src/lib/swarm-layout.ts, and more — 11,272 lines total against 69,257 in src. Additionally App.tsx:4 imports LaunchScreen and declares `launchMode` state (App.tsx:15) that are never used (TS6133 when noUnusedLocals is enabled). Running tsc with --noUnusedLocals --noUnusedParameters produces 150 unused-symbol errors. This is classic AI-generated accretion: features rewritten in place with the old version left behind.
findings.recommendation: Delete all 34 files (git preserves history), remove the dead LaunchScreen import/state, then turn on noUnusedLocals/noUnusedParameters in tsconfig.json and add knip or ts-prune to CI so unreferenced modules fail the build.

findings.title: Duplicate electron-vite configs: electron.vite.config.ts is dead but silently wins if --config is omitted
findings.description: Both electron.vite.config.ts and electron.vite.config.mjs exist with byte-for-byte identical structure differing only in `__dirname` vs `import.meta.dirname`. Every package.json script hardcodes `--config electron.vite.config.mjs`, making the .ts file dead — but electron-vite's default config resolution PREFERS the .ts file, so anyone running bare `npx electron-vite dev` (as release.yml:31 does with `npx electron-vite build`!) uses the OTHER config. Today they happen to match; the first divergent edit creates a works-locally-breaks-in-CI split. Note the CI workflow already builds with no --config flag, so CI is actually building via the .ts config while local scripts use .mjs.
findings.recommendation: Delete electron.vite.config.mjs, keep the single electron.vite.config.ts (electron-vite handles TS configs natively), and drop all --config flags from package.json scripts so local and CI provably run the same config.

findings.title: Four dead npm dependencies shipped in the dependency tree: ansi-to-html and all three @dnd-kit packages (plus unused @electron/rebuild)
findings.description: `ansi-to-html` (package.json:37) has zero imports anywhere in src/ or electron/ — only package-lock references. `@dnd-kit/core`, `@dnd-kit/sortable`, `@dnd-kit/utilities` (package.json:30-32) also have zero imports; tab drag-reorder either doesn't exist or was reimplemented manually, and the abandoned TerminalTabs.tsx doesn't use them either. devDependency `@electron/rebuild` (line 55) is never invoked — the rebuild script uses `electron-builder install-app-deps`, and electron-builder bundles its own rebuild. These are production `dependencies`, so they inflate install time and supply-chain surface for every user.
findings.recommendation: Remove ansi-to-html, @dnd-kit/*, and @electron/rebuild from package.json. Add `npx knip` or depcheck to CI to keep the manifest honest.

findings.title: Window.ghostshell type is hand-duplicated from preload instead of derived, and has already drifted
findings.description: electron/preload.ts:122 exports `export type GhostShellAPI = typeof api` — the canonical, always-correct type of the bridge — but nothing imports it. Instead src/lib/types.ts:293-347 re-declares the entire ~45-method API by hand. It has already drifted: `toggleFullscreen` (preload.ts:9) is missing from the Window type, forcing `(window as any).ghostshell?.toggleFullscreen?.()` casts in CommandPalette.tsx:412 and useKeyboardShortcuts.ts:295; `updaterInstall` is typed `() => void` (types.ts:338) while preload returns an ipcRenderer.invoke Promise (preload.ts:99). Every future preload addition requires remembering to update two places or the renderer loses type safety for that method.
findings.recommendation: Replace the manual block with `import type { GhostShellAPI } from '../../electron/preload'` and `declare global { interface Window { ghostshell: GhostShellAPI } }`, then delete the two `as any` escape hatches. Single source of truth for the IPC surface.

findings.title: tsconfig gaps: unused-code flags off, main process type-checked with DOM lib, tsconfig.node.json configured to emit into electron-vite's out/ directory
findings.description: Three issues: (1) tsconfig.node.json sets `noEmit: false` with `outDir: './out'` — running `tsc -p tsconfig.node.json` without an explicit --noEmit emits stray .js files directly into the same out/ directory electron-vite uses for its bundles (main entry is out/main/index.js), risking stale-file confusion; there is no reason for tsc to emit at all in an esbuild pipeline. (2) tsconfig.node.json doesn't restrict `lib`, so main-process code inherits default DOM typings — `document`/`window` references in electron/ would type-check fine and crash at runtime. (3) The base config lacks noUnusedLocals/noUnusedParameters (150 violations exist), noUncheckedIndexedAccess, and noFallthroughCasesInSwitch; @types/node is not a direct devDependency (relied on transitively via electron).
findings.recommendation: Set noEmit:true and `"lib": ["ES2022"]`, `"types": ["node"]` in tsconfig.node.json; add @types/node explicitly pinned to Electron's Node version; enable noUnusedLocals/noUnusedParameters after the dead-code purge and noUncheckedIndexedAccess for the regex/array-heavy parser code.

findings.title: Renderer ships as one 2.68 MB unminified chunk with no sourcemaps; intended code-splitting is defeated by mixed static/dynamic imports
findings.description: The production build emits assets/index-*.js at 2,681 kB containing fully readable unminified source (verified by inspecting the bundle) and zero sourceMappingURL entries — worst of both worlds: slow parse on startup and no debuggability benefit that sourcemaps would give. Vite prints three warnings that swarm-self-heal.ts, swarm-autonomy.ts, and swarm-knowledge-graph.ts are dynamically imported (by swarm-orchestrator.ts, swarm-activity-emitter.ts, SwarmSimulationView.tsx) but ALSO statically imported (by usePty.ts, SwarmRightPanel.tsx, SwarmAutonomyConfig.tsx, SwarmDashboard.tsx, swarm-simulator.ts), so the dynamic imports split nothing — those modules land in the main chunk anyway while 13 other swarm chunks split correctly.
findings.recommendation: Enable minify ('esbuild') and sourcemap:true for the renderer in electron.vite.config; make the static-vs-dynamic import decision consistent per module (usePty statically importing swarm-self-heal is the main offender — invert it or accept eager loading and drop the dynamic imports). Add manualChunks for xterm/framer-motion/lucide to keep the entry chunk lean.

findings.title: Terminal fonts loaded from Google Fonts CDN at runtime; CSP whitelists a leftover perplexity.ai domain
findings.description: index.html pulls Inter and JetBrains Mono from fonts.googleapis.com at runtime (built output confirms the <link> survives to production). Offline or behind a proxy, the terminal renders in fallback monospace — glyph metrics change, meaning xterm.js cell measurement and grid layout differ between online and offline launches of a desktop app. The CSP font-src also whitelists `https://r2cdn.perplexity.ai` (index.html CSP meta, visible at out/renderer/index.html line 6), a domain nothing in the app uses — copied-config residue that widens the trust surface for no reason.
findings.recommendation: Self-host both fonts (npm: @fontsource/inter, @fontsource/jetbrains-mono) so Vite bundles them, tighten CSP to font-src 'self', and delete the perplexity.ai entry. WezTerm bundles JetBrains Mono for exactly this determinism reason.

findings.title: Three overlapping release paths with divergent publish semantics
findings.description: Releasing can happen via (a) `npm run release` → electron-builder `--publish always` using electron-builder.yml's publish block (owner candrei8), (b) the CI workflow which runs `--publish never` and then manually crafts the release with `gh release delete/create` uploading dist/*.exe + latest.yml, or (c) manual electron-builder. The manual gh path recreates what electron-builder publish already does, and `gh release delete "$TAG" --yes` silently destroys any existing release for the tag — re-running the workflow can wipe a live release's assets between delete and create. dev-app-update.yml duplicates the publish coordinates a third time.
findings.recommendation: Pick one path: let electron-builder publish (`--publish always` in CI with GH_TOKEN) and delete the manual gh-release steps and the local `release` script, or vice versa. One tool must own latest.yml generation or auto-update will eventually point at a mismatched artifact.

findings.title: electron-builder file exclusions use single-star globs and reference nonexistent files; mac/linux targets configured but never built
findings.description: files exclusions `!src/*` and `!electron/*` (lines 7-8) use single-star patterns that match only direct children in minimatch terms — nested sources like src/components/** may still be packed into the asar, bloating the installer with raw TS source (unverified against a built artifact — flagging for verification with `npx asar list`). Line 10 excludes .eslintrc.cjs/.prettierrc.yaml which do not exist in this repo (template residue). The mac (entitlements plist) and linux (AppImage) sections are dead weight: only a Windows workflow exists and build/entitlements.mac.plist is referenced but untested.
findings.recommendation: Switch to an explicit allowlist (`files: ['out/**']` plus package.json) which is the electron-builder best practice, verify the asar contents once, and delete the untested mac/linux sections until there is CI to build them.

findings.title: ensure-electron-install.js wired into 7 pre-scripts plus postinstall; stale browserslist data warning on every build
findings.description: The same guard script runs as predev, prebuild, prepreview, prerebuild, prepackage, prerelease, ensure:electron AND postinstall — eight registrations for one idempotent check, adding startup latency to every command and lots of script noise. Separately, every production build prints 'Browserslist: browsers data (caniuse-lite) is 6 months old', meaning autoprefixer targets stale browser data (harmless for Electron's fixed Chromium, but the warning masks real ones).
findings.recommendation: Keep only postinstall (the script exists to fix broken installs, which happen at install time) and one explicit `ensure:electron` escape hatch; run `npx update-browserslist-db@latest` or pin a `browserslist: ['Chrome 130']` entry matching the Electron version so prefixing is exact.

research.summary: Researched WezTerm's mux/pane source (mux/src/tab.rs), VS Code's terminal architecture (pty host, FlowControlConstants in src/vs/platform/terminal/common/terminal.ts, shellIntegration.ps1, process revive), xterm.js official guides (flow control, WebGL/serialize/fit addons), and Warp/Ghostty block systems. Key verified facts: WezTerm models panes as a binary tree (leaves = panes, internal nodes = SplitDirectionAndSize{direction, first, second} with a 1-cell divider) with recursive proportional resize and an out-of-tree zoom slot; VS Code isolates node-pty in a dedicated pty-host process with ack-based flow control (HighWatermarkChars=100000, LowWatermarkChars=5000, CharCountAckSize=5000), persists terminals by running xterm-headless + SerializeAddon inside the pty host, and replaces regex prompt sniffing with OSC 633/133 sequences injected into PowerShell by wrapping the global Prompt function and PSConsoleHostReadLine; Warp builds blocks from precmd/preexec shell hooks (equivalent to OSC 133 A/B/C/D boundaries) storing {command, output, exit code, cwd, timestamp} per block. Sources: https://deepwiki.com/wezterm/wezterm/2.2-multiplexer-architecture, https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wezterm/wezterm/main/mux/src/tab.rs, https://wezterm.org/copymode.html, https://github.com/wezterm/wezterm/discussions/5394, https://deepwiki.com/microsoft/vscode/6-integrated-terminal, https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/113827, https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/terminal/shell-integration, https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/terminal/advanced, https://raw.githubusercontent.com/microsoft/vscode/main/src/vs/workbench/contrib/terminal/common/scripts/shellIntegration.ps1, https://xtermjs.org/docs/guides/flowcontrol/, https://github.com/xtermjs/xterm.js/blob/master/addons/addon-webgl/README.md, https://github.com/xtermjs/xterm.js/blob/master/addons/addon-serialize/README.md, https://code.visualstudio.com/updates/v1_60, https://www.warp.dev/blog/how-warp-works, https://ghostty.org/docs/install/release-notes/1-3-0, https://deepwiki.com/ghostty-org/ghostty/9.3-osc-133-prompt-marking.

recommendations.pattern: WezTerm's Tab holds `Tree = bintree::Tree<Arc<dyn Pane>, SplitDirectionAndSize>`: leaves are panes, internal nodes carry `SplitDirectionAndSize { direction: Horizontal|Vertical, first: TerminalSize, second: TerminalSize }`. Helpers `top_of_second()`/`left_of_second()` derive child offsets; `width()`/`height()` include a 1-cell divider. New splits go through `compute_split_size(SplitRequest{ size: Cells(n)|Percent(p), target_is_second })`: requested size to one child, remainder minus divider to the other. Divider drag = `resize_split_by()` locating the split node, mutating `first.cols`/`first.rows` clamped to [1, total - divider - 1], then `cascade_size_from_cursor()` walks descendants calling `pane.resize()` on each leaf. Window resize = recursive `adjust_x_size()`/`adjust_y_size()` distributing the delta proportionally with per-pane minimums, then `apply_sizes_from_splits()`. Note: Wez keeps the tree private because it's an implementation detail he plans to change — the serializable mirror is `PaneNode::{Empty, Split{left,right,node}, Leaf(PaneEntry)}`.
recommendations.applicability: Model each GhostShell tab as a plain JSON binary tree in a renderer store (e.g. `type SplitNode = { kind:'leaf', terminalId } | { kind:'split', direction, ratio, first, second }`). Render with absolutely-positioned divs computed by one pure `layoutTree(node, rect)` function (mirrors top_of_second/left_of_second) rather than nested flexbox — this makes divider hit-testing, zoom overlay and serialization trivial. On divider drag update `ratio`, recompute layout, then for every affected leaf call FitAddon.fit() and send `pty.resize(cols, rows)` over IPC (this is the cascade step). Store ratios as floats but clamp resulting cells to >=1 row/col like WezTerm's saturating clamp. Because the tree is plain JSON (unlike WezTerm's hidden tree) tab-layout persistence is free: save the tree + per-leaf serialized buffers.

recommendations.pattern: Zoom does NOT mutate the tree. `TabInner` keeps `zoomed: Option<Arc<dyn Pane>>` plus `size_before_zoom: TerminalSize`. `toggle_zoom()` resizes the target pane to full-tab size and sets the slot; un-zoom restores `size_before_zoom` and re-applies tree sizes. `iter_panes()` returns only the zoomed pane while zoomed; `iter_panes_ignoring_zoom()` sees the real tree.
recommendations.applicability: Add `zoomedTerminalId: string | null` alongside the split tree — never restructure the tree to zoom. When set, render only that pane's container at full tab size (CSS: absolutely position it over the whole tab area, keep sibling xterm DOM mounted but hidden), call fit() + pty.resize to full dimensions; on un-zoom re-run layoutTree and resize back. Keep the other panes' xterm instances alive (do not dispose) so their buffers and WebGL textures survive the toggle.

recommendations.pattern: WezTerm's copy mode (Ctrl+Shift+X) is a modal overlay over the pane's scrollback: vim movement (h/j/k/l, w/b, 0/$, Ctrl+F/B/D/U), three selection modes — cell (v), line (V), block/rectangular (Ctrl+V) — `y` copies and exits, Esc/q exits without copying; bindings live in a dedicated `copy_mode` key table, and search mode integrates with it. Title is prefixed 'Copy Mode' as a mode indicator.
recommendations.applicability: Implement as a per-pane keyboard mode flag: when active, `attachCustomKeyEventHandler` swallows all keys and drives a virtual cursor using xterm.js APIs — `term.select(col, row, len)` / `term.selectLines(start, end)` for cell/line modes, `term.scrollLines()` for viewport movement, `term.getSelection()` + `navigator.clipboard.writeText()` on 'y'. Render the copy-mode cursor with `term.registerDecoration({ marker })`. Block selection needs manual per-row select + join on copy (xterm.js has no rectangular selection). Show a 'COPY MODE' badge in the pane header as the mode indicator. This is high-value for an AI-agent terminal because agents produce long outputs users need to grab keyboard-only.

recommendations.topic: Process isolation: dedicated PTY host process (VS Code)
recommendations.pattern: VS Code runs all node-pty instances in a separate 'pty host' Node process, never in the renderer and not in the main process. Motivation (issue #74620): node-pty crashes were taking down the renderer, and fast producers starved its event loop. The renderer-side `TerminalProcessManager` talks to the pty host's `PtyService` over IPC; the pty host owns shell lifecycle, IO, flow control, capabilities, and persistence, and survives renderer reloads. A heartbeat detects pty-host hangs/crashes and it can be restarted without killing windows.
recommendations.applicability: In Electron 33 use `utilityProcess.fork('ptyHost.js')` from main: node-pty runs there with full Node APIs, isolated from both main and renderer. Wire renderer<->ptyHost directly with `MessageChannelMain` + `postMessage({...}, [port])` so terminal data skips the main process entirely (one hop, no main-thread jank). Protocol: `{type:'spawn'|'data'|'input'|'resize'|'ack'|'exit', id, ...}`. Give every terminal a persistent numeric id assigned by the pty host (not the renderer) so reconnection after a renderer reload is `attach(id)` rather than respawn. Add a ping/heartbeat from main; if the pty host dies, restart it and mark terminals as needing revive.

recommendations.topic: Flow control between pty and renderer (VS Code + xterm.js official guide)
recommendations.pattern: Ack-based flow control, exact VS Code constants from `FlowControlConstants`: `HighWatermarkChars = 100000` (unacknowledged chars before the pty is paused), `LowWatermarkChars = 5000` (resume threshold), `CharCountAckSize = 5000` (chars accumulated client-side before sending an ack). Renderer counts chars it has fully processed — using the `term.write(chunk, callback)` completion callback — and sends an ack every 5000 chars; the pty host tracks unacked chars, calls `pty.pause()` above 100k and `pty.resume()` below 5k. The xterm.js flow-control guide confirms the write-callback watermark approach (example HIGH=100000/LOW=10000) and recommends attaching callbacks only every ~100KB to reduce overhead, since xterm parses at 5-35 MB/s while producers can push GB/s.
recommendations.applicability: This is the single most important pattern for an AI-agent terminal (agents cat huge files / run verbose builds). In ptyHost: `onData` -> post chunk, `unacked += chunk.length; if (unacked > 100000) pty.pause()`; on `ack` message `unacked -= n; if (paused && unacked < 5000) pty.resume()`. In renderer: `term.write(chunk, () => { pendingAck += chunk.length; if (pendingAck >= 5000) { port.postMessage({type:'ack', n: pendingAck}); pendingAck = 0; } })`. node-pty's pause()/resume() work on Windows/ConPTY. Also batch: coalesce pty data events in the pty host with a ~5ms flush timer into larger messages to cut postMessage overhead (VS Code's 'event batching').

recommendations.topic: Terminal persistence, reconnection and revive (VS Code)
recommendations.pattern: Because ptys live in the pty host, a window reload just re-attaches: `LocalReconnectConstants { GraceTime = 60000, ShortGraceTime = 6000 }` — a detached process is kept alive 60s awaiting reconnect. Buffer restore evolved from replaying recorded raw data events to running a headless xterm (`@xterm/headless`) per terminal inside the pty host, writing all pty output to it, and on reattach sending `SerializeAddon.serialize()` output (full ANSI, colors preserved) as a replay event. Full app restart uses 'process revive': serialize buffer + shell config + cwd/env to disk (`ISerializedTerminalState`), then relaunch the shell and prepend the restored buffer; scrollback restored is tunable (`terminal.integrated.persistentSessionScrollback`, default ~100 lines) to balance speed vs fidelity.
recommendations.applicability: In GhostShell's pty host, per terminal create `new HeadlessTerminal({ scrollback })` + SerializeAddon and mirror all pty data into it (cheap, and it doubles as the source for command-block text extraction). Renderer reload flow: renderer asks `listTerminals()`, then `attach(id)` -> pty host replies with `serialize()` string -> renderer writes it to the fresh xterm before resuming live data (queue live data until replay write's callback fires to preserve ordering). App restart flow: on quit, persist `{splitTree, terminals: [{id, cwd, shell, serializedBuffer}]}` to disk; on launch, respawn ptys and write a dim 'restored' banner + serialized buffer. This gives tab restore without keeping Electron alive.

recommendations.topic: Shell integration: OSC 633/133 instead of regex prompt sniffing (VS Code, FinalTerm standard)
recommendations.pattern: Semantic sequences mark command lifecycle: `OSC 633;A ST` prompt start, `OSC 633;B ST` prompt end/command-line start, `OSC 633;C ST` pre-execution (output begins), `OSC 633;D;<exitcode> ST` command finished, `OSC 633;E;<commandline>;<nonce> ST` explicit command line, `OSC 633;P;Cwd=<path> ST` property reporting (also `IsWindows`, `HasRichCommandDetection`). OSC 133;A/B/C/D is the vendor-neutral FinalTerm equivalent (A=prompt start, B=command start, C=command executed, D=finished) supported by Ghostty/WezTerm/iTerm2. VS Code injects scripts automatically at shell launch via args/env; quality tiers None/Basic/Rich.
