Exit codes drive command decorations (success/fail circles in gutter + scrollbar) and Ctrl+Up/Down command navigation.
recommendations.applicability: Adopt OSC 133 A/B/C/D as GhostShell's canonical protocol (also accept 633 so VS Code's scripts work as-is). In the renderer register parsers BEFORE opening: `term.parser.registerOscHandler(133, data => ...)` and `registerOscHandler(633, ...)`; on 'A' drop `term.registerMarker(0)` as prompt marker, on 'C' mark output start, on 'D;code' close the current command record with exit code. Build a per-terminal `CommandDetection` store: `{promptMarker, commandLine, executedMarker, endMarker, exitCode, cwd}` — this replaces every regex prompt heuristic and is exactly what an AI agent needs to know 'command X finished with code Y, output is lines M..N'. Note Claude Code and most agents don't emit these; the shell does, so it works for anything run inside the shell.

recommendations.topic: PowerShell injection of shell integration (VS Code shellIntegration.ps1)
recommendations.pattern: The script saves the user prompt (`$Global:__VSCodeState.OriginalPrompt = $function:Prompt`) and installs a new global `Prompt` that emits, in order: `D;<exitcode>` for the previous command (exit code computed as `$FakeCode = [int]!$global:?`, with `if ($FakeCode -ne 0) { Write-Error "failure" -ea ignore }` afterwards to restore `$?` for the user's own prompt logic), then `A` (prompt start), then `P;Cwd=<escaped $pwd.ProviderPath>`, then invokes the original prompt text, then `B` (prompt end). Command-line capture wraps PSReadLine's `PSConsoleHostReadLine`: after the user submits a line it emits `E;<escaped commandline>;<nonce>` then `C` just before execution. A nonce is read from `$env:VSCODE_NONCE` at startup and the env var is immediately cleared, so decorations can't be spoofed by program output. Injection is automatic at launch (VS Code passes the script via shell args/env).
recommendations.applicability: Ship a `ghostshell-integration.ps1` doing exactly this (emit OSC 133 A/B/C/D + a private OSC for Cwd, or just reuse 633 format). Inject on spawn Windows-first: `node-pty.spawn('pwsh.exe', ['-NoLogo','-NoExit','-Command','. "C:\...\ghostshell-integration.ps1"'], { env: {...process.env, GHOSTSHELL_NONCE: nonce } })` — works for powershell.exe 5.1 and pwsh 7. Critical details to copy: always wrap (never replace) an existing user Prompt; restore `$?` after computing the fake exit code; escape semicolons/backslashes in Cwd and command line values (`__VSCode-Escape-Value` equivalent); validate the nonce renderer-side before trusting `E` command lines. Fallback tiering like VS Code: if no A/B/C/D seen within N seconds mark the terminal 'basic' and disable block features rather than falling back to regex.

recommendations.topic: Command blocks (Warp) and block features on top of OSC 133 (Ghostty)
recommendations.pattern: Warp: every command+output is a Block object `{command, stdout/stderr, exit code, cwd, timestamp}` built from precmd/preexec shell hooks (zsh/fish native; bash via bash-preexec) that send a DCS-encoded JSON to the terminal; blocks are independently copyable/bookmarkable/shareable, color-coded by exit status (red sidebar for non-zero), and unattributed output becomes 'background blocks'. Ghostty deliberately avoids a block UI but its OSC 133 implementation powers jump-to-prompt, copy-command-output, prompt-aware resize (reflow only the active prompt region) and the new click-to-move-cursor-in-prompt (cl=line extension).
recommendations.applicability: GhostShell can get 90% of Warp blocks without abandoning the xterm grid, using the OSC 133 markers already collected: (1) gutter decorations — `term.registerDecoration({ marker: promptMarker })` rendering a solid sky-400 bar for running, solid red bar for exitCode!=0 (fits the no-glow/no-gradient style guide); (2) 'copy output' = read buffer lines between the C marker and D marker via `term.buffer.active.getLine(y).translateToString()`; (3) Ctrl+Up/Down jump = `term.scrollToLine(marker.line)`; (4) 'rerun' = `term.paste(commandLine)`; (5) expose blocks to the AI agent as structured JSON ({command, exitCode, outputText, cwd, durationMs}) — this is the killer feature for an agent terminal: the agent queries block history instead of scraping the screen. Skip Warp's custom renderer; marker+decoration over xterm.js is the proven low-cost path (it is exactly what VS Code does).

recommendations.topic: xterm.js renderer lifecycle: WebGL addon with fallback
recommendations.pattern: Official guidance: load WebglAddon after `term.open()`; the browser can drop WebGL contexts (OOM, suspend/resume, GPU reset), so you MUST handle `addon.onContextLoss(e => { addon.dispose(); })` — disposing falls back to the DOM renderer; @xterm/addon-canvas exists as an intermediate fallback. VS Code additionally caps the number of live WebGL contexts (browsers limit ~8-16 contexts) and recreates the addon when a terminal becomes visible again.
recommendations.applicability: Per pane: `const webgl = new WebglAddon(); webgl.onContextLoss(() => { webgl.dispose(); /* optionally retry once after 3s, else stay on DOM renderer */ }); term.loadAddon(webgl)` — only AFTER `term.open(el)`. Since GhostShell can have many panes/tabs, don't keep a WebGL context per hidden tab: on tab hide, `webgl.dispose()`; on tab show, load a fresh WebglAddon (buffer state is unaffected, only rendering). This dodges Chromium's context limit and the suspend/resume context-loss bug class (vscode issue #263159). Dispose order on pane close: addons via term.dispose() (it disposes loaded addons), then remove the DOM node, then tell pty host to kill or orphan the pty.

recommendations.topic: xterm.js sizing: FitAddon + ResizeObserver + pty resize
recommendations.pattern: Canonical loop: `term.open(el); fitAddon.fit(); new ResizeObserver(() => fitAddon.fit()).observe(el)`. fit() calls `proposeDimensions()` (container size / cell size) then `term.resize(cols, rows)`. Known pitfalls from xterm.js issues: fit() on a hidden/zero-size element yields NaN/undefined dimensions; resize feedback loops when the observer fires during layout; and the pty must be resized too or full-screen apps (nvim/tmux) misrender (issue #3873).
recommendations.applicability: Wrap it: on ResizeObserver callback, `const d = fitAddon.proposeDimensions(); if (!d || !d.cols || !d.rows || Number.isNaN(d.cols)) return;` then fit(), and drive the pty from xterm's own `term.onResize(({cols, rows}) => port.postMessage({type:'resize', id, cols, rows}))` — single source of truth, fires only on real changes. Debounce the observer ~50-100ms (rAF-align) to avoid ConPTY resize storms during divider drags (ConPTY reflow on Windows is expensive; send the final size, not every intermediate). Never fit() panes in hidden tabs — refit on tab activation instead. Spawn the pty with the initial `term.cols/term.rows` from the first successful fit.

recommendations.topic: xterm.js input handling: onData vs custom key handlers, bracketed paste
recommendations.pattern: Division of labor used by VS Code: `term.onData(d => pty.write(d))` is the ONLY path for terminal input — xterm.js already encodes keys, IME composition, and mouse reports into correct escape sequences (`onBinary` for the rare binary mouse path). `attachCustomKeyEventHandler(ev => boolean)` runs BEFORE xterm processes a key and is exclusively for app-level shortcuts: return false to steal the key from the terminal (copy/paste, tab/pane navigation, copy-mode entry), true to let xterm handle it. Paste must go through `term.paste(text)`, which normalizes newlines to \r and honors bracketed paste mode (DECSET 2004) by wrapping in ESC[200~ / ESC[201~ when the running app enabled it.
recommendations.applicability: GhostShell rules: (1) never synthesize escape sequences yourself — pipe onData verbatim to node-pty; (2) implement Ctrl+Shift+C/V, Ctrl+Tab, pane-focus keys, and copy-mode activation in attachCustomKeyEventHandler returning false for those combos (Electron menu accelerators alternatively work but the handler gives per-pane control and works when the menu is hidden); (3) route clipboard paste through term.paste() so multi-line AI-generated commands pasted into pwsh/PSReadLine arrive as one bracketed paste instead of executing line-by-line — this is a real safety issue for an AI-agent terminal; consider a confirm dialog when pasted text contains \n and the target has bracketed paste OFF (VS Code and iTerm2 both warn); (4) IME/dead keys on Windows: rely on onData, do not use onKey for input.

recommendations.pattern: SerializeAddon serializes the terminal framebuffer to a string of ANSI escape sequences (or HTML) — `serializeAddon.serialize({ scrollback })`; writing that string into a fresh Terminal reproduces content, colors, and cursor state. It's the preferred restore path in VS Code (color-preserving) with plain `translateToString()` as a colorless fallback; VS Code limits restored scrollback (default ~100 lines) because serialize/replay cost scales with buffer size. Officially 'experimental' but shipped in VS Code production for years.
recommendations.applicability: Load SerializeAddon in the pty host's headless terminals (see persistence pattern), not in the renderer — the renderer copy is redundant. Cap serialized scrollback (100-1000 lines, user setting) for restore speed; store alongside `{cols, rows}` and `term.resize` to those dims BEFORE writing the replay so wrapping matches, then fit() to current size after. For GhostShell's AI features, `serialize()` is also the clean way to hand the agent a faithful snapshot of 'what's on screen' including SGR state, and `serializeAsHTML()` gives you export/share-block-as-rich-text for free.

verdicts.title: Checkpoint/rollback silently destroys untracked files (git clean -fd on state never captured)
verdicts.reason: Verified. main.ts:432-449 checkpoints via `git stash create`, which by design captures only tracked modifications + index — untracked files are never in the stash object (there is no -u form of `stash create`). main.ts:452-467's dirty-rollback path then runs `git checkout .` + `git clean -fd` + `git stash apply <hash>` in that order, so every untracked non-ignored file — including ones that existed untracked at checkpoint time — is permanently deleted, and the wipe happens BEFORE `stash apply`, so a failed apply leaves the tree already shredded. The doc comment in src/lib/swarm-checkpoints.ts:145-146 falsely claims this 'restores the exact working tree state at that point'. In an app whose agents create new (untracked-until-committed) files, this is silent unrecoverable data loss in the flagship rollback feature. One inaccuracy in the claim: SwarmRollbackPanel.tsx:52-57 DOES implement a two-click confirm (5s auto-dismiss), so 'no confirmation' is overstated — but the confirm never mentions untracked deletion and there is no backup/dry-run, so the substance and critical severity stand.

verdicts.title: Zero PTY output flow control or coalescing — one webContents.send per node-pty chunk
verdicts.reason: Verified. main.ts:280-282 does `mainWindow?.webContents.send(`pty:data:${id}`, data)` inside pty.onData with no batching; a grep of electron/ finds zero uses of IPty.pause()/resume() or any flow-control/ack mechanism. The renderer handler at usePty.ts:759-880 is confirmed heavy per chunk: imageLabels.maskText, sanitizeReadOnlyDisplay, optional enhanceTerminalOutput, stripAnsi + two \r normalizations, provider-detection regexes, two CWD regexes, commandBlockStore.appendOutput (Zustand set per chunk), batchParser.push, companion accumulation, and a `window[bufferKey]` assignment — all before xterm even paints. Minor nuance vs the claim: the export buffer is capped at 50K (usePty.ts:742-743, 810-812) and block output at 24K chars (commandBlockStore.ts:36), so 'unbounded memory growth' applies chiefly to xterm's internal write queue when the renderer falls behind, not to those buffers. The absence of any backpressure between node-pty and the renderer is real and high severity is justified for a terminal emulator.

verdicts.title: sandbox:false + unrestricted filesystem/exec IPC surface with zero sender validation
verdicts.reason: Verified as stated. main.ts:185 sets sandbox:false while preload.ts imports only contextBridge, ipcRenderer, and webUtils — all fully functional in a sandboxed preload, so nothing requires the setting. The IPC surface is confirmed unscoped: fs:createFile (main.ts:470), fs:delete (525), fs:readFile (548) accept arbitrary absolute paths with no workspace-root check; pty:create (256-293) passes a free-form `shell` string that pty-manager.ts:29-38/200 tokenizes and spawns directly (arbitrary exe execution); cli:getVersion (719-731) and cli:discoverModels (710-716) run an arbitrary caller-supplied command via runCommand; git:rollback runs `clean -fd` in any cwd. Every handler names its event `_event` — no senderFrame/sender validation anywhere. Mitigating context: contextIsolation:true, nodeIntegration:false, and only local content is loaded, so exploitation requires prior renderer compromise — this is a defense-in-depth gap, not a directly reachable vuln. But because the bridge amounts to arbitrary exec + full-disk read/write/delete from the renderer, high remains the right rating per standard Electron hardening guidance.

verdicts.title: force-device-scale-factor=1 breaks every high-DPI Windows machine
verdicts.reason: Verified. main.ts:44 appends `force-device-scale-factor=1`, forcing Chromium to render the whole app at 96 DPI regardless of Windows display scaling, and main.ts:43's `high-dpi-support` is a Chromium switch removed years ago (no-op on Electron 33). No compensation exists anywhere: webPreferences pins zoomFactor:1.0 (main.ts:188), there is no devicePixelRatio handling in src/ (grep confirms), and the app is frameless with no menu, so default zoom accelerators are unlikely to be available; the only mitigation is a 10-18px terminal/UI font-size setting (settingsStore.ts:263,300) which does not fix hit targets, layout, or per-monitor DPI switching. On the typical 125-150% scaled Windows display — the app's primary platform per its own ConPTY-first design — everything renders undersized. App-wide visual defect on the primary platform: high is justified.

verdicts.title: Recreating a session with the same id can deliver the OLD process's exit event to the NEW session
verdicts.reason: Verified, and the triggering scenario is more common than the claim implies. Mechanics all check out: main.ts:280-286 registers per-create onData/onExit closures that are never disposed and send on dynamic `pty:data:${id}`/`pty:exit:${id}` channels; pty-manager.ts:153-156 kills any same-id process on create; the guard at pty-manager.ts:212-217 protects only the internal Map, not main.ts's sends. The renderer registers its exit listener only after the awaited pty:create resolves (usePty.ts:746 → 1462), so a late exit from the old process (ConPTY exit notification on Windows is routinely delayed tens to hundreds of ms) lands on the NEW listener, which prints '[Process exited]' (usePty.ts:1467), finalizes the active block as 'interrupted' (1472), and sets the agent offline (1483) while the new PTY is alive. Same-id recreation demonstrably occurs in normal use: TerminalContainer.tsx:108-152 keys the pane subtree by workspace in tabs mode but by 'grid-view' in grid mode, so toggling view modes remounts every TerminalPane; usePty's cleanup calls ptyKill(sessionId) (usePty.ts:1570) and the remount re-creates the PTY with the SAME session.id 50ms later (usePty.ts:1548-1550) — exactly the race window. Late pty:data bleed from the dying process is equally possible. High severity is appropriate.

verdicts.title: MultiLineInput submits with the backslash+CR sequence that usePty's own comment documents as buggy
verdicts.reason: Code-level facts all verified: handleMultiLineSubmit (TerminalPane.tsx:280-296) writes '\\' then '\r' per line for Claude; provider defaults to 'claude' with no agent/detectedProvider (TerminalPane.tsx:274-276); usePty.ts:196-204 documents that exact approach as broken and uses '\x1b\r'; terminalPromptSubmission.ts:23-26,59-61 also uses '\x1b\r'. HOWEVER the harm scenario is unreachable: the overlay's only opener is the SHORTCUT_EVENTS.openMultiLineInput listener (TerminalPane.tsx:203-209, sole setMultiLineOpen(true) site), and NOTHING dispatches that event — verified across useKeyboardShortcuts.ts, CommandPalette.tsx, usePty.ts, all of src/, and even the built bundle (out/renderer/assets/index-oZXtBXxW.js has only the listener). There is no 'Ctrl-shift-multiline' binding; the real multiline shortcut is Shift+Enter (shortcutRegistry.ts:556-562 'xterm.multiline'), which routes through usePty.ts:1072-1075 writeMultilineShortcut and the CORRECT '\x1b\r' sequence. So the 'PowerShell executes each line immediately' scenario cannot happen in the shipped app. Downgraded high→low: it is a real defect (orphaned dead code carrying the documented-broken protocol, a booby trap if anyone wires it up), not a live input-corruption bug. The fix recommendation (route through submitPromptToSession, or delete the component) is still correct.

verdicts.title: MultiLineInput submissions invisible to history, command blocks, and companion log
verdicts.reason: Accurately read at the code level: handleMultiLineSubmit (TerminalPane.tsx:270-306) writes raw ptyWrite calls and never calls registerPromptSubmission, while the command bar path (TerminalCommandBar.tsx:932 submitTypedCommand → submitPromptToSession → registerPromptSubmission at terminalPromptSubmission.ts:87-98) records into historyStore, commandBlockStore, and companionStore. BUT the described data inconsistency cannot manifest: the MultiLineInput overlay is dead code — no code path ever dispatches SHORTCUT_EVENTS.openMultiLineInput (verified in src/ and in the built bundle), so no user prompt can ever flow through handleMultiLineSubmit and bypass the stores. Multiline prompts entered via the only live surfaces (command bar, Shift+Enter in xterm) ARE registered or are raw terminal input by design. Downgraded high→low: real code-quality defect in an unreachable handler (same root cause as the previous claim — both would be fixed by deleting the orphaned overlay or wiring it through submitPromptToSession), not a live 'silent data inconsistency'.

verdicts.title: QuickLaunch directory autocomplete is 100% broken on Windows (builds /C:/... paths, verified ENOENT)
verdicts.reason: Fully confirmed, including empirically. The autocomplete effect (QuickLaunchRedesign.tsx:317-379) builds parentDir as '/' + norm.join('/') (lines 353-357), so 'C:\projects\gh' → '/C:/projects' and relative input against a 'C:\Users\chitu' base → '/C:/Users/chitu/...'. api.fsReadDir passes the string unmodified to fs.readdir in the main process (electron/main.ts:316-318, no normalization). Reproduced on this machine with Node 22: readdirSync('/C:/Users') → ENOENT and path.resolve('/C:/Users') → 'C:\C:\Users'. The catch at line 324/360 swallows the error, so suggestions silently stay empty for every drive-letter path — i.e. every real Windows path. Also confirmed: renderer fallback finalPath = '/' + resolved.join('/') at line 144, and both drive-letter regexes (lines 132, 339) lack the 'i' flag (verified: /^[A-Z]:[/\\]/ rejects 'c:/foo', misparsing it as relative). One precision note: the submit-time resolveInputPath is mitigated in production by the shellResolvePath IPC tried first (lines 109-115, handler at main.ts:772), so it is specifically autocomplete — which never uses the IPC — that is always broken. High severity stands: a primary-flow feature (new-session QuickLaunch) is completely non-functional on the owner's only platform, Windows 11.

verdicts.title: QuickLaunch home-directory fallback has no Windows branch and explicitly discards Windows workspace paths
verdicts.reason: Code accurately described: the homeDir detector (QuickLaunchRedesign.tsx:248-290) has no C:\Users branch; the inference regex at line 261 matches only /Users|/home prefixes; the /Users probe (266-276) uses a macOS skip-list plus single-dir heuristic (on this Windows machine C:\Users has 9 entries, so it never resolves — the probe does accidentally read C:\Users drive-relatively, but the heuristic fails anyway); and line 294 confirms the anti-Windows filter !/^[A-Z]:\\/.test(currentPath). '(works after full Electron restart)' comments confirmed at lines 108 and 252 (claim cited 111/253, trivially off). Severity over-rated though: the IPC shellGetHomedir is tried FIRST (line 254) and its handler exists (electron/main.ts:770, app.getPath('home')), so in any production build homeDir resolves correctly on Windows and the missing-Windows-branch fallbacks are dev-hot-reload dead weight, not a broken production path. The only permanent Windows defect is the line-294 filter, which merely degrades the default-folder fallback from the workspace currentPath to homeDir — projectPath from lastAgentFolder (lines 218-220) and typed paths still work. Minor extra wart the auditor missed: that filter only matches backslash-style 'C:\...' so a forward-slash 'C:/...' currentPath slips through, making the exclusion inconsistent as well as wrong-headed. Downgraded high→medium: real Windows-hostile code worth deleting, but user impact is a suboptimal default, not breakage.

verdicts.title: enhanceTerminalOutput injects SGR into escape sequences split across chunk boundaries, garbling Claude Code's TUI
verdicts.reason: Verified. The enhancer is stateless per chunk (terminalOutputEnhancer.ts:133-147) and the per-line ESC guard at line 118 cannot see an ESC byte that arrived in the previous IPC chunk; electron/main.ts:280-281 forwards each ConPTY onData read verbatim with no re-chunking or partial-sequence carry (pty-manager.ts confirms no coalescing). xterm's VT parser is streaming, so a pending \x1b from chunk N followed by injected '\x1b[1m\x1b[95m' from the enhancer aborts the original sequence and renders '[2K' as literal text — exactly the claimed corruption. It is ON by default (settingsStore.ts:306 terminalOutputEmphasis:'balanced') and applied only to Claude (usePty.ts:768-774 bypasses gemini/codex). One correction to the auditor's example: a continuation chunk consisting solely of '[2K\rReading foo.ts' (contains \r, no \n) is skipped by the guard at line 141, and any chunk containing '\x1b]' is skipped wholesale by line 140 — these guards reduce frequency but do not fix the cross-chunk statelessness; real multi-line repaint chunks pass both guards. Critical stands for a terminal emulator: the default-on feature intermittently corrupts the flagship provider's rendering, and the timing-dependence matches the reported intermittent artifacts.

verdicts.title: imageLabels.maskText rewrites raw PTY data with different-length text, desyncing TUI column math
verdicts.reason: Verified mechanism, overrated severity. usePty.ts:766 runs imageLabels.maskText(data) on every raw output chunk, and the masked result is what gets written to xterm (lines 767-806), so a ~55-char temp path echoed by Claude Code's input box renders as 7-char 'Image 1' while the CLI computes borders/wrap points against the real length — the alignment breakage claim is real. Also confirmed: masking is chunk-local (terminalImageLabels.ts:25-36, no carry state), so paths split across IPC chunks leak through; labelsByPath is never cleared (lines 12-23); and 3 new RegExp objects are compiled per label per chunk in the hot path (lines 28-32). Downgraded from critical to high because: (a) it only activates after the user pastes/drops an image (labels added only at usePty.ts:1200 and 1390 — with no labels the loop is a no-op), (b) it corrupts only the displayed rows containing the path, not the PTY input stream (the real bytes were already written to the PTY at usePty.ts:1201; maskText at line 519 affects only history/echo bookkeeping), and (c) it is a scoped, deliberate cosmetic feature rather than an always-on stream corruptor like the enhancer.

verdicts.title: Regex-triggered auto-confirm blindly types 'y\r' into agent PTYs
verdicts.reason: Verified exactly as claimed. usePty.ts:868-882: for any agent session (if (agentId)), every raw output chunk is tested against getAutoConfirmPatterns(currentProvider) and on match ptyWrite(sessionId, 'y\r') fires 150ms later. There is no settings gate anywhere in the block (defaultSkipPermissions in settingsStore is never consulted here), no user confirmation, and no notification. The patterns are as loose as claimed: CLAUDE_AUTO_CONFIRM_PATTERNS at usePty.ts:48-58 include /\(y\)es.*\(n\)o/i, /\? \(Y\/n\)/ and /\? \(y\/N\)/ — the last one auto-answers YES to prompts whose printed default is NO. Gemini's patterns (lines 86-90) are even worse: bare /\(y\/n\)/i and /Do you want to proceed/i. Any agent that merely PRINTS such text (reading a README, cat-ing a script, running an installer) gets 'y' + Enter injected into its input box, either corrupting the conversation or silently approving an interactive child-process prompt. Critical is justified: this is unsanctioned keystroke synthesis that can defeat confirmation/permission prompts with zero opt-out.

verdicts.title: Keyword-based line classification recolors ordinary prose; nested wraps half-paint lines
verdicts.reason: Every sub-point verified in terminalOutputEnhancer.ts. (1) detectHighlightKind line 70 marks any line containing error|failed|not found|denied as 'error' → bold red / red background, so prose like 'this handles the error case' recolors. (2) CONTEXT_LINE_VALUE_PATTERN (line 39, checked at line 68) matches bare '$5', '12 tokens', 'Turn 3' anywhere in a line → bold cyan 'context' styling. (3) ACTION_PATTERN (line 28, applied at line 104) recolors bare English words (Read, Running, Done via SUCCESS_PATTERN line 32) mid-prose. (4) Nested-reset bug confirmed: enhanceLine line 122 runs enhanceInlineTokens first (injects COLOR...\x1b[0m per token via wrap() at lines 41-43), then line 130 wraps the whole mutated line; each inner \x1b[0m resets ALL attributes including the vivid-mode background from wrapImportantLine (lines 88-94), producing half-painted highlight bars. (5) Guard gap confirmed: line 141 only skips chunks with \r AND no \n, so a split part containing a bare \r plus the chunk's \r\n elsewhere is wrapped as one styled unit. (6) Dead ternary confirmed at line 100 (both branches `${BOLD}${INFO}`). High is the right severity for a default-on visual-correctness defect.

verdicts.title: createBatchParser re-parses its 200-char tail and TUI repaints re-feed identical text, duplicating events and sub-agents
verdicts.reason: Verified. claude-output-parser.ts:872 retains the last 200 chars after every parse tick, so any match sitting in that tail is re-detected on each subsequent 100ms batch until new data pushes it out; combined with Claude Code's full-screen repaints re-transmitting identical tool-call text, duplicate ParseResults are structurally guaranteed. Consumer defenses match the claim: sub-agent spawn dedupe is only a 1200ms window (SUBAGENT_SPAWN_DEDUPE_MS at usePty.ts:419, checked at 707-710 — and note a duplicate outside the window first COMPLETES the previous sub-agent at 713-716 before spawning a phantom); addFileTouch (usePty.ts:639), addEvent (641), and companion.addActivityEvent (642-648) have zero dedupe; every non-idle result bumps lastWorkingPatternTime (line 624), distorting the idle detector. The BUFFER_MAX slice at lines 858-859 (buffer.slice(-2000)) can indeed cut an escape sequence mid-body, leaving fragments like '[0;35m' with no leading ESC that ANSI_STRIP (line 5) cannot remove. High severity is appropriate: it floods the activity/telemetry features and idle detection but does not corrupt the terminal itself.

verdicts.title: stripAnsi misses DEC private modes and ST-terminated OSC, leaking control bytes into parsed text and Companion chat
verdicts.reason: Verified by regex inspection. ANSI_STRIP at claude-output-parser.ts:5 is /\x1b\[[0-9;]*[a-zA-Z]|\x1b\].*?\x07|\x1b\(B/g: the class [0-9;]* cannot consume '?', so '\x1b[?25l', '\x1b[?2026h', '\x1b[?1049h' (all ubiquitous in TUI output) survive stripping entirely. OSC handling only matches BEL-terminated sequences; an ST-terminated OSC ('\x1b]0;title\x1b\\') either leaks whole or, worse, the lazy .*?\x07 over-consumes legitimate text up to a later BEL. accumulateCompanionOutput at usePty.ts:578-588 pipes this same 'stripped' text line-by-line into companion.addAssistantMessage, where the ESC byte is invisible in HTML and the user sees literal '[?25l'-style fragments. The downstream-regex-pollution point is also sound since unstripped OSC payloads (window titles containing cwd paths) flow into the loose parser patterns. High is correct: it degrades the Companion chat and parser reliability for default features.

verdicts.title: 'Formal' tool-call regexes target an output format Claude Code doesn't print, while ALT fallbacks fire on arbitrary prose
verdicts.reason: The code-verifiable half is fully confirmed and damning on its own. TOOL_READ and siblings (claude-output-parser.ts:8-16) require literal `Read(file_path: "...")` key:value syntax; there are zero captured fixtures or tests in the repo backing that format (only fileDrop/swarm/imageLabels/textInput/terminalStore tests exist), so the primary patterns are unvalidated guesses. The ALT false positives are provable from the regexes: TOOL_READ_ALT (line 29) /(?:📖|Reading)\s+([^\s\n]+)/ turns 'Reading more about X' into fileTouch path 'more'; CODEX_SHELL_ALT (line 601) has /i and no \b so 'gran torino' matches 'ran' and records running_bash 'torino'; GEMINI_READ_ALT (line 399) matches the bare word 'Read' anywhere. The one hedge: whether the formal patterns 'essentially never match' depends on each CLI version's rendering (Claude Code's expanded/verbose views have historically shown parameter key:value forms), which cannot be confirmed from this repo alone — the auditor appropriately flagged this as unverified. Either way the finding stands: the pipeline feeds file-history/activity features a mix of unvalidated primary matches and provable prose garbage. High is correct.

verdicts.title: Context metrics regexes ingest '$1' and 'N tokens' from arbitrary output as cost/token telemetry
verdicts.reason: Verified end-to-end. COST_PATTERN at claude-output-parser.ts:43 is /\$(\d+(?:\.\d+)?)/ with no anchoring, so any '$1' in script output (awk, bash positional params — extremely common in agent output) sets costEstimate=1 in extractContextUpdate (lines 94-129, cost assigned at 110-112). TOKENS_PATTERN (line 42) matches prose like 'uses 5 tokens' and overwrites tokenEstimate (lines 107-109). These flow into a real ParseResult whenever ANY of the four patterns matches (line 100), then usePty.ts:659-685 calls updateContextMetrics and emits 'Context: ...' system messages into Companion chat (deduped only against the immediately-previous summary at line 681, so alternating false values still spam). The enhancer independently recolors '$1' via CONTEXT_PATTERN at terminalOutputEnhancer.ts:30. High is fair: it systematically corrupts a headline UI gauge (context/cost) from ordinary output, though it causes no functional damage beyond wrong telemetry.

verdicts.title: Shipped test suite fails: terminalTextInput test asserts behavior the implementation deliberately removed
verdicts.reason: Reproduced, not just accepted: running `npx vitest run src/lib/__tests__/terminalTextInput.test.ts` yields 1 failed / 2 passed. The failing assertion is exactly terminalTextInput.test.ts:10-12 (expects insertFromPaste/insertReplacementText/insertFromDrop → true) versus the implementation at terminalTextInput.ts:22-26 which only returns true for multi-char 'insertText', with a comment explicitly stating insertFromPaste is deliberately not intercepted. The 'zero tests for terminalOutputEnhancer and claude-output-parser' addendum is confirmed by globbing src/**/__tests__ (only fileDrop, swarm-integration, terminalImageLabels, terminalTextInput, terminalStore). Downgraded to medium: the implementation change was correct and the stale test has zero runtime impact on users; the real cost is the process signal (a permanently-red suite means tests gate nothing), which is a quality/process finding rather than a high-severity product defect.

verdicts.title: Multi-line prompts sent to plain shells use Claude's ESC+CR sequence, wiping lines in PSReadLine
verdicts.reason: Verified. getPromptProvider at terminalPromptSubmission.ts:14-21 returns session?.detectedProvider || 'claude', so a plain PowerShell tab (no agentId, no detected provider) resolves to 'claude'; writePrompt (lines 50-62) then joins multi-line commands with getNativeMultilineSequence('claude') = '\x1b\r' (line 24) in a single ptyWrite. In PSReadLine (the default shell path — pty-manager.ts:22-27 spawns powershell.exe on win32), Escape clears the current input line, so the payload 'line1\x1b\rline2\x1b\rline3\r' types line1, wipes it, submits empty, and ultimately executes only the final line — silently. That is worse than cosmetic: executing the last line of a multi-line script without its preceding lines (variable assignments, cd, guards) can run a destructive tail command in the wrong context. All four cited callers confirmed reachable with provider-less sessions via grep and reading: TerminalCommandBar.tsx:932, HistoryPanel.tsx:29 (activeSessionId, any session), SettingsModal.tsx:135, CommandBlocksPanel.tsx:146. High is correct — silent command corruption, but requires the multi-line-into-plain-shell path rather than affecting every keystroke.

verdicts.title: 368 Tailwind opacity-modifier classes compile to NOTHING — app-wide typography hierarchy is silently broken
verdicts.reason: CONFIRMED empirically. I compiled a probe file with the project's own Tailwind 3.4.19 and tailwind.config.js: text-ghost-text-dim/40, border-ghost-border/70, bg-ghost-border/50, bg-ghost-surface/60, bg-ghost-error/10, bg-ghost-sidebar/50, bg-ghost-text-dim/20, bg-ghost-border/40 all produced ZERO CSS output, while text-ghost-text/60 and bg-ghost-accent/10 (the two rgb-triplet tokens, tailwind.config.js:15,17) compiled correctly. My own grep found 352 occurrences across 41 files (auditor said 368 — same magnitude, immaterial delta). ResizeHandle.tsx:45-47 confirmed: both rest-state classes (bg-ghost-border/40, bg-ghost-text-dim/20) are dropped so the grip is invisible at rest; minor overstatement only in that hover:bg-ghost-accent/40 and group-hover:bg-ghost-accent/60 DO work (accent has a triplet), so it appears on hover. Critical is justified: pervasive, silent, app-wide visual failure of the design-token system.

verdicts.title: Invalid white/black opacity steps are dropped, and border-white/8 elements fall back to preflight's LIGHT GRAY #e5e7eb borders

Compilation with the project's Tailwind 3.4.19 verified that border-white/8, bg-white/3, bg-white/4, border-white/6, border-white/12, bg-black/22, bg-black/28 and all text-white/16..92 non-multiple-of-5 steps generate no CSS, while /5, /10, /40 compile. The compiled base layer contains preflight `border-color: #e5e7eb` on *, and globals.css has no override (its `*` reset at line 35 sets only margin/padding/box-sizing). All cited lines verified verbatim: TerminalContextPanel.tsx:73/74/99/114/136/148/152/156 use border-white/8, and the panel IS live (rendered at TerminalPane.tsx:586). MarkdownPreview.tsx:270/286/291, StructuredDataPreview.tsx:99/217, FilePreview.tsx:128, SwarmDirectoryStep.tsx:55 and the TerminalCommandBar text opacities all check out. However total scope is 36 invalid classes (15x border-white/8), i.e. ~8 components — glaring where present (1px light-gray lines on a near-black panel) but localized, unlike the 352-instance claim above. High, not critical.

verdicts.title: Workspace tab right-click menu is clipped to invisibility by the titlebar's overflow-hidden
verdicts.reason: CONFIRMED. GlobalDock.tsx:218 root is `relative z-20 flex h-11 ... overflow-hidden`; ContextMenu renders inside it (lines 220-226); ContextMenu.tsx:33-34 is `absolute` positioned with left/top from e.clientX/e.clientY (set at GlobalDock.tsx:253). Since the dock is the positioned ancestor AND the overflow-hidden clip container, an 11-item menu (9 TAB_COLORS + Default + Rename, ~300px) opened at y≈15-35 inside a 44px-tall container is clipped to a sliver — the color feature is effectively unusable. Severity overstated though: rename remains reachable via double-click (GlobalDock.tsx:252), so only the secondary tab-color feature is fully lost. A broken secondary context menu is high, not critical.

verdicts.title: Style-guide violations: 3 CSS gradients and a colored glow shadow, in an app whose own comments say 'no gradients, no glows'
verdicts.reason: CONFIRMED with one path nit. Grep found exactly the three gradients: TerminalCommandBar.tsx:989 (linear-gradient background), TerminalContextPanel.tsx:73 (bg-[linear-gradient(180deg,...)]), FilePreview.tsx:430 (radial + linear stacked). The glow is real but the file is src/components/agents/ContextGauge.tsx:49 (not swarm/) — `boxShadow: `0 0 6px ${statusColor}40`` verified at that line. animate-ping/animate-pulse confirmed in 16 files (TerminalPane.tsx:383, SwarmHeader.tsx:65, SwarmStatusTimeline.tsx:104, ShortcutsTab.tsx:295, etc.), and the ironic 'Glass UI, no gradients, no glows' headers exist (SwarmApprovalQueue.tsx:3, SwarmAutonomyConfig.tsx:3, SwarmDebrief.tsx:4). All are direct CLAUDE.md violations, but purely cosmetic with zero functional impact — medium, not high.

verdicts.title: Font pipeline is broken: UI font never loaded, terminal bold is faux, fonts come from a CDN, no Nerd Font fallback
verdicts.reason: CONFIRMED on every point. index.html:10 loads Inter 300-700 + JetBrains Mono 300-600 (no 700) from Google Fonts; the UI stack is 'Manrope, Segoe UI Variable Text, ...' (globals.css:47, tailwind.config.js:27) and Manrope appears nowhere else — no @font-face, no fontsource, no local .woff/.ttf files anywhere in the repo (glob verified). 'Inter' is referenced by zero source files, so the download is pure waste. useTerminal.ts:163 sets fontWeightBold '700' while JBM 700 is not requested — synthesized bold confirmed. Default terminal stack 'JetBrains Mono, Fira Code, Cascadia Code, Consolas, monospace' (settingsStore.ts:301) has no Nerd Font/Symbols fallback. package.json has @xterm/addon-webgl but no ligatures addon. CSP at index.html:6 whitelists r2cdn.perplexity.ai in font-src — verified leftover. For a terminal app whose core output is text, high is the right severity.

verdicts.title: SwarmViewToggle floats over the window controls — can cover the only Close button of the frameless window
verdicts.reason: CONFIRMED. SwarmViewToggle.tsx:16-17 is `fixed right-3 z-[60]` with style top:6 — a ~200px-wide two-button pill spanning y≈6-38. AppLayout.tsx:305 renders it whenever isSwarmActive, and GlobalDock is ALWAYS rendered above it in the tree (AppLayout.tsx:276) with the h-11 (44px) titlebar at z-20 containing Settings/Minimize/Maximize/Close as h-9 w-9 buttons at the right edge (GlobalDock.tsx:310-351) — those occupy roughly the same band (y≈4-40, rightmost ~185px). electron/main.ts:179-180 confirms frame:false + titleBarStyle:'hidden' with no titleBarOverlay, so these HTML buttons are the only pointer-accessible window controls. Both elements share the root stacking context; z-[60] > z-20 so the toggle intercepts clicks over Close/Maximize whenever a swarm is active. High is correct (Alt+F4 still works and it only occurs mid-swarm, so not critical).

verdicts.title: Hardcoded colors defeat the 16-theme system: 275x #38bdf8 in components, purple Electron background, opaque hex titlebar and settings modal
verdicts.reason: CONFIRMED, with one trivial nit. Grep counts exactly 275 occurrences of #38bdf8 in src/**/*.tsx across 40 files, plus 68x #ef4444. Verified verbatim: bg-[#080c14] titlebar (GlobalDock.tsx:218), settings modal background '#0c1020' (SettingsModal.tsx:311), tab fallback '#4094e0' (GlobalDock.tsx:49,56) which indeed appears nowhere in TAB_COLORS (closest is #3d8ae0), AgentHUD bg-[#0a0f1a]/95 (AgentHUD.tsx:45), Logo hardcoding #38bdf8/#1A1B26 (GlobalDock.tsx:62-63). BrowserWindow backgroundColor '#1a1025' (electron/main.ts:181) is RGB(26,16,37) — a purple tint matching neither qubria-dark's '#0f1729' (themes.ts:8) nor the :root fallback '#050912' (globals.css:16). Only nit: themes.ts defines 15 themes, not 16. The theming system genuinely only restyles part of the UI; high is correct.

verdicts.title: ~640 lines of dead visual components: TerminalTabs, LaunchScreen, FloatingSidePanel — plus duplicated tab logic in two live/dead copies
verdicts.reason: CONFIRMED but over-rated. TerminalTabs.tsx is 366 lines with zero external imports and duplicates GlobalDock's tab machinery with a 7-entry Spanish-labeled TAB_COLORS ('Rojo', 'Naranja'... lines 40-46), its own getAutoColor (line 51) and 'Renombrar' menu (line 147). LaunchScreen.tsx (235 lines) is imported at App.tsx:4 and launchMode state declared at App.tsx:15, but App renders only <AppLayout/> — both dead; 'v1.7.0' at LaunchScreen.tsx:220 vs package.json version 2.2.0 verified. verdicts.title: globals.css is ~35% dead: entire dock-*, ql-*, glass-panel and shortcut-key blocks style components that no longer exist
verdicts.reason: CONFIRMED but over-rated. I grepped every named class against all src *.ts/*.tsx: dock-bar, dock-git-pill, dock-new-btn, dock-icon-btn, ql-root, ql-launch-btn, ql-specialist-card, ql-templates-scroll, ghost-glass-panel(-strong), ghost-shortcut-key(-muted), sidebar-transition, resize-handle, terminal-container — all ZERO references. Line ranges verified (dock block globals.css:318-355, ql block 364-414, glass panels 145-159, shortcut keys 190-216, sidebar-transition 110-113, resize-handle 288-301); dead total ≈160 of 415 lines ≈ 38%, matching '~35%'. ghost-app-shell::before transparent overlay + `> * { z-index: 1 }` confirmed at globals.css:131-143 (ghost-app-shell itself IS used, AppLayout.tsx:275). terminal.css claims verified: .terminal-container (49-55) unused; `.terminal-pane .xterm { flex: 1 }` (64-66) is a genuine no-op because .xterm's parent is the non-flex `absolute inset-0` mount div (TerminalPane.tsx:536). Real rot, but zero user-facing impact — medium, not high.

verdicts.title: Custom keyboard shortcuts never persist: StateStorage passed where PersistStorage is required
verdicts.reason: Verified mechanically against installed zustand 5.0.11: persist calls storage.setItem(name, {state, version}) with an OBJECT (node_modules/zustand/esm/middleware.mjs:358); electronStorage.setItem (src/lib/electronStorage.ts:28) runs JSON.parse on it, which throws on '[object Object]' and is swallowed at :35-37 — nothing is ever written. On hydrate, middleware.mjs:388-405 reads .version/.state off the JSON string getItem returns, gets undefined, and defaults win. shortcutStore.ts:339 is the only store passing the raw adapter ('storage: electronStorage as any'); all six other persisted stores wrap with createJSONStorage (settingsStore.ts:368, workspaceStore.ts:151, historyStore.ts:245, modelStore.ts:334, swarmStore.ts:1121). ShortcutsTab.tsx really exercises assignBinding/resetAll/repairConflicts, so user rebinds are silently lost on restart. Severity corrected critical→high: it is silent loss of one settings feature's configuration, with no crash, no data corruption outside shortcut prefs, and no impact on live terminal work.

verdicts.title: Maximize and tabs/grid view-switch unmount panes and kill their live PTYs
verdicts.reason: Fully confirmed. PTY lifetime is coupled to React mount: usePty's effect cleanup unconditionally calls window.ghostshell.ptyKill(sessionId) (usePty.ts:1570), remount re-creates via ptyCreate (usePty.ts:746) after a 50ms StrictMode-guard timer (:1548-1550), and pty-manager.create() kills any existing same-id process (electron/pty-manager.ts:153-155). BentoLayout.tsx:59-65 renders ONLY the maximized pane, unmounting every sibling TerminalPane (TerminalPane.tsx:147 hosts usePty directly — no persistent xterm/PTY registry exists). The maximized pane itself also remounts: the keyed slot is reused (div, same session-id key) but its child flips between BentoLayout's wrapper div (grid branch, :78) and the TerminalPane element directly (maximize branch), a host-vs-component type change that forces remount. The tabs/grid toggle (TerminalTabs.tsx:100/107) is equally confirmed: TerminalContainer.tsx:121-122 keys the wrapper by first-session-id in tabs mode but by the literal 'grid-view' in grid mode, so every pane remounts and every shell/agent restarts. The author demonstrably knew the invariant (stable-key comment TerminalContainer.tsx:115-120; 'Terminals always stay mounted to keep PTY sessions alive' AppLayout.tsx:291-293) and only patched the split-promotion case. Critical is justified: a routine UI action destroys live agent processes and all their context.

verdicts.title: Three uncoordinated keyboard layers: rebindable registry, hardcoded xterm intercepts, and a rogue Ctrl+Space listener
verdicts.reason: All three layers verified in code. Layer 1: useKeyboardShortcuts.ts:60 bails on event.defaultPrevented and :29 deliberately treats .xterm as non-editable (bubble-phase window keydown, :505). Layer 2: usePty.ts:1026-1125 attachCustomKeyEventHandler hardcodes Ctrl+T (:1112-1117 dispatches newTerminal regardless of registry), F2 (:1120-1122), Shift+Enter (:1074), Ctrl+V (:1082), and Ctrl+C variants (:1030/:1036/:1089/:1096) — none consult shortcutStore, so a rebound 'New Terminal' keeps firing on Ctrl+T in-terminal. Layer 3: TerminalContainer.tsx:28-37 is a raw window keydown for Ctrl+Space with no defaultPrevented or editable-target check, opening AgentHUD even while typing in inputs/modals, while a focused xterm simultaneously sends NUL. The per-combo lottery is real: registry defaults tab.1-9 = Ctrl+1..9 (shortcutRegistry.ts:524-530) and tab.prev/next = Ctrl+PageUp/PageDown (:499/:506); xterm's evaluateKeyboardEvent translates Ctrl+2..8 to NUL/ESC/FS/GS/RS/US/DEL control bytes and preventDefaults (killing layer 1), while Ctrl+1/Ctrl+9 are unmapped and bubble through — so tab 3 (Ctrl+3) sends ESC, which can cancel a running Claude prompt. High is justified for a keyboard-driven terminal app: stray control bytes reach agent CLIs and rebinding is unreliable whenever a terminal has focus.

verdicts.title: Async persist hydration is never awaited: restoreTabs race and theme/font flash on every launch
verdicts.reason: The architectural fact is true — grep confirms zero uses of hasHydrated/onFinishHydration/persist.rehydrate anywhere, AppLayout.tsx:133 reads restoreTabs in a mount effect that races async IPC hydration, and App.tsx:17-19/:78-80 apply the default theme/fontSize before settingsStore.ts:399-406 re-applies persisted values. But the headline HIGH consequence is refuted: the 'user who disabled tab restore still gets tabs restored' scenario is effectively unreachable, because snapshots are written ONLY in onBeforeClose (App.tsx:26-40) using the post-hydration (correct) restoreTabs value, and are deleted both immediately after every startup restore (AppLayout.tsx:139 — directly contradicting the auditor's assertion that 'clearTabSnapshot only runs on graceful close') and on graceful close when the setting is off (App.tsx:37). A crash writes no snapshot at all, so no stale snapshot can coexist with persisted restoreTabs=false via the described path. What survives is a race-timing-dependent cosmetic theme/typography flash on cold start (real but unproven to occur 'on every launch' — hydration IPC may well complete before first paint) plus a latent read-before-hydration hazard. That is a polish/robustness issue, not high: corrected to low.

verdicts.title: commandBlockStore never releases data for closed sessions (unbounded growth across the app's lifetime)
verdicts.reason: Confirmed leak: blocksBySession/activeBlockBySession (commandBlockStore.ts:23-24) have no teardown tied to session close. usePty's unmount cleanup (usePty.ts:1552-1574) removes the activity record (:1560) and companion session (:1568) but never touches command blocks; terminalStore.removeSession (terminalStore.ts:199-208) only adjusts sessions/groups/active ids; clearSession is invoked solely from the manual panel button (CommandBlocksPanel.tsx:174-175). Even clearSession sets the key to [] rather than deleting it. Blocks are created on every prompt submission (terminalPromptSubmission.ts:82) and stream all PTY output through appendOutput (usePty.ts:815), so closed agent sessions do retain real data. Severity corrected high→medium: growth is capped per session (300 blocks, 24k output + 36k rawOutput chars each — worst case ~36 MB as UTF-16, realistically far less since most blocks are small), only accumulates across many opened-and-closed sessions within one app run, is fully reclaimed on restart, and causes no functional breakage — a genuine slow memory leak, not a high-impact defect.

verdicts.title: All 'open settings tab' shortcuts land on the Appearance tab due to `??` after a void optional call
verdicts.reason: Confirmed and deterministic. useKeyboardShortcuts.ts:439/:447/:455/:463 all use `onOpenSettingsTab?.(tab) ?? onNavigate?.('settings')`; AppLayout.tsx:249 supplies onOpenSettingsTab (returns void → undefined), so the nullish-coalescing RHS always executes too: handleNavigate('settings') (AppLayout.tsx:79-82) calls openSettings() with the default 'appearance' (AppLayout.tsx:57-60). Both setSettingsTab calls batch in the same keydown handler, so the final settingsTab is 'appearance', and SettingsModal seeds and follows initialTab (SettingsModal.tsx:87, :173-175). Net: the Terminal/Providers/Shortcuts settings shortcuts always open on Appearance (nav.settings itself is unaffected since it passes 'appearance' anyway). Severity corrected high→medium: the settings modal still opens and the intended tab is one click away — a real, clearly-diagnosed functional bug defeating three shortcuts' purpose, but with trivial impact and workaround.

verdicts.title: Shipped TypeScript error is a runtime ReferenceError that breaks Enter in plain-shell sessions
verdicts.reason: Verified end-to-end. (1) tsc reproduces: `npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.web.json` fails with exactly `src/hooks/usePty.ts(523,7): error TS2304: Cannot find name 'inputBuffer'`. (2) Scope structure confirmed: trackCommandSubmission is declared at usePty.ts:502 in the useEffect scope; the only `let inputBuffer = ''` is at line 950 inside `const init = async () => {}` (line 736) — invisible to trackCommandSubmission. (3) Shipped bundle confirmed: out/renderer/assets/index-oZXtBXxW.js line 45228 has `let inputBuffer2 = ""` (Rollup deconflict rename) while line 44878 keeps a bare `inputBuffer = "";` with NO declaration of `inputBuffer` anywhere in the bundle; index.html loads it as `<script type="module">` (strict mode), so the assignment throws ReferenceError. (4) Propagation confirmed: xterm 5.5's EventEmitter.fire has no try/catch (`for(...) i[s].call(void 0,e,t)`), so the throw escapes the onData callback at usePty.ts:1428 and the `\r` forwarding at 1441-1451 never runs, after registerPromptSubmission (line 521) already created a command block. In sessions with no agentId and no detectedProvider (isInteractiveProviderSession, usePty.ts:402-405), any typed non-provider command can NEVER be executed — every Enter re-throws. Minor overstatement only: an empty Enter early-returns at line 504 without throwing, and provider sessions take the safe else branch at 1430; but the claim already scopes itself to plain-shell sessions. A terminal app whose plain terminal tabs cannot run commands, shipped in the v2.2.0 production bundle, is correctly rated critical.

verdicts.title: No typecheck, test, or lint gate anywhere in the build or release pipeline
verdicts.reason: Verified. .github/workflows/release.yml is the ONLY workflow (glob confirmed) and its steps are exactly: npm ci (line 24) → npx electron-vite build (line 29) → npx electron-builder (line 32) → gh release create (lines 40-48). No test, typecheck, or lint step. package.json scripts (lines 7-25) contain only build/package/test scripts — no `typecheck` or `lint` entry. No ESLint/Prettier config exists at the repo root (glob for .eslintrc*/eslint.config.*/.prettierrc* matched only node_modules), yet electron-builder.yml:10 excludes `.eslintrc.cjs`/`.prettierrc.yaml` — copied-template residue as claimed. `npm_config_node_linker: hoisted` is at release.yml:26 (auditor said 27 — off by one, immaterial); `node-linker` is a pnpm option npm ignores. The consequence is proven, not hypothetical: the TS2304 error (claim 1) and the failing test (claim 3) both shipped in v2.2.0. High is justified.

verdicts.title: Test suite is permanently red: stale test asserts behavior the implementation deliberately removed
verdicts.reason: Verified by execution: `npm test` at HEAD exits 1 with exactly '1 failed | 85 passed (86)', the failure being 'captures structured paste and replacement input types' in src/lib/__tests__/terminalTextInput.test.ts. Lines 10-12 expect shouldCaptureStructuredTextInsertion('insertFromPaste'|'insertReplacementText'|'insertFromDrop', 'hello') === true, but src/lib/terminalTextInput.ts:22-26 only returns true for insertType 'insertText' with length > 1, and the comment at lines 18-21 explicitly documents that intercepting insertFromPaste was deliberately removed because it caused double paste writes. The test was never updated for the intentional behavior change. Keeping high within the tests-build domain: a suite that is red on a clean checkout has zero signal value, makes any future CI gating (claim 2's fix) impossible without this fix, and normalizes ignoring failures. No runtime user impact, but as test-infrastructure health it is a top-tier defect.

verdicts.title: Zero test coverage for every terminal-critical module; vitest config makes main-process and DOM testing impossible
verdicts.reason: Every factual assertion checked out exactly. Line counts verified with wc -l: usePty.ts 1576, useTerminal.ts 394, electron/pty-manager.ts 298, claude-output-parser.ts 886, terminalOutputEnhancer.ts 147, terminalStore.ts 655. Only 5 test files exist (fileDrop, swarm-integration, terminalImageLabels, terminalTextInput, terminalStore), so usePty/useTerminal/pty-manager/claude-output-parser/terminalOutputEnhancer have 0 tests. src/stores contains 13 stores; only terminalStore is tested, and terminalStore.test.ts contains a single describe('terminalStore.closeWorkspace') with exactly 3 it() cases (lines 40-77). vitest.config.ts:7 sets environment 'node' and line 8 sets include to 'src/**/__tests__/**/*.test.ts', which structurally excludes electron/** — pty-manager cannot be picked up as configured. jsdom is not installed (node_modules/jsdom absent) and @testing-library appears nowhere in package.json, so hook/component tests are impossible without config+dependency changes. Given that the untested code is the heuristic-heavy core that already shipped a critical runtime bug (claim 1), high is the right rating.

verdicts.title: `electronStorage as any` passes the wrong storage interface to zustand persist — shortcut overrides silently never persist
verdicts.reason: Verified against both the app code and zustand 5.0.11's actual source. shortcutStore.ts:339 is `storage: electronStorage as any` while all other persisted stores wrap it: historyStore.ts:245, modelStore.ts:334, settingsStore.ts:368, swarmStore.ts:1121 (and workspaceStore.ts:151) all use createJSONStorage(() => electronStorage). electronStorage (src/lib/electronStorage.ts:8) is a string-based StateStorage whose setItem does JSON.parse(value) at line 28 with a swallow-all catch at line 35. zustand's persist middleware (node_modules/zustand/esm/middleware.mjs:358) calls `storage.setItem(options.name, { state, version })` with a raw OBJECT when given a PersistStorage — createJSONStorage (line 298) is the layer that would have stringified it. So JSON.parse receives an object, coerces to "[object Object]", throws SyntaxError, caught at line 35 → console.error only, and the localStorage fallback at lines 32-34 is unreachable after the throw → writes never happen. On hydration (middleware.mjs:388-405), getItem's return value is used directly: `.version` on a string is undefined (not number) → else branch returns `[false, deserializedStorageValue.state]` → `.state` of a string is undefined → merge with undefined is a no-op. Both directions broken exactly as claimed; custom shortcuts are silently lost on restart, and the `as any` cast is what suppressed the TS2322 that would have flagged it. High is correct: silent user-data loss in one feature, not app-breaking.

verdicts.title: Electron 33.4.11 is past end-of-life with 18 unpatched advisories; js-yaml moderate DoS in prod deps
verdicts.reason: Verified by running the tools. Installed electron is exactly 33.4.11 (node_modules/electron/package.json); `npm audit --omit=dev` reports 'electron <=39.8.4, Severity: high' with exactly 18 advisories, including both specifically cited ones — ASAR Integrity Bypass (GHSA-vmqv-hx8q-j7mg) and Windows registry key path injection in setAsDefaultProtocolClient (GHSA-mwmh-mq4g-g6gr) — plus multiple use-after-frees and HTTP response header injection; fix suggests electron@43.1.0 as claimed. js-yaml 4.1.1 moderate quadratic DoS (GHSA-h67p-54hq-rp68) confirmed, and `npm ls js-yaml --omit=dev` shows it is pulled in solely via electron-updater@6.8.3 (which parses latest.yml). The remote-content claim is also true: src/index.html:7-10 (and the shipped out/renderer/index.html) preconnect to and load Google Fonts stylesheets/fonts, with CSP explicitly allowing fonts.googleapis.com/fonts.gstatic.com plus a third origin (r2cdn.perplexity.ai). Electron 33 (Chromium 130) left the 3-supported-majors window in 2025, so 'no security backports for over a year as of July 2026' is accurate. Only defect in the claim is the citation package.json:55 — electron is declared at package.json:52 (line 55 is postcss); immaterial. High is appropriate: real EOL-Chromium exposure in a shell-spawning app, but exploitation still requires a concrete vector, so not critical.
